signals.summary: Claude Desktop writes session registry entries (local_<sid>.json) with a non-atomic in-place write. If the process dies during fsync, the file ends up with correct size but all-null bytes. The .jsonl transcript is intact but the session is silently dropped from /resume, session picker, and all MCP list_sessions tools. Pinned custom titles and conversation history become unreachable.
aliases: session file corrupted crash null bytes
signals.review_reason: Critical data loss: crash mid-write silently destroys session registry entry. The conversation transcript is intact on disk but permanently unreachable through all UI surfaces. Requires manual hex-repair of JSON schema — far beyond normal user recovery. Pinned sessions and custom titles permanently lost. Three related issues (#24958, #24009, #23421) were closed stale without resolution.

source_issues.title: Registry file written non-atomically: Claude Desktop crash mid-write produces all-null `local_*.json`, session vanishes from picker (Windows 1.7196.0.0)
source_issues.evidence: Concrete forensic evidence: 144,258-byte all-null registry file with intact 38.5 MB .jsonl transcript. Session vanished from /resume, picker, and all MCP tools. Manual recovery required patching JSON schema by hand. Recurring bug (related issues #24958, #24009, #23421 closed stale). No recovery UI or warning logged.

signals.topic: Skill tool broken in headless (`claude -p`) mode since v2.1.141 — returns is_error, skill body never loaded, CI/automation workflows degraded
signals.summary: Since v2.1.141, invoking skills via the Skill tool in `claude -p` / print mode returns is_error: true with content 'Execute skill: <name>' instead of 'Launching skill: <name>'. The skill body is never loaded into context. This is a regression (v2.1.140 works). Model-independent — affects both Opus and Haiku. Impacts CI pipelines, headless orchestration, and multi-agent workflows that rely on skills.
aliases: headless mode skill tool regression v2.1.141
Skill tool fails in print mode
signals.review_reason: Regression in headless/CI mode: skill execution silently fails in `claude -p` since v2.1.141. While interactive mode works, headless/automation workflows — a core use case — are broken. ~95 previously-working skill invocations broke on upgrade. Bisected to specific version boundary. Model-independent per reporter.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Skill tool broken in headless (`claude -p`) mode since v2.1.141 — returns is_error, skill body never loaded
source_issues.evidence: Bisected across 5 versions: v2.1.139-140 work, v2.1.141-143 broken. Reporter had ~95 successful headless skill invocations across v2.1.112-139, all broken at once on upgrade. Model-independent (reproduced with both Opus and Haiku). CI/headless orchestration workflows silently degrade — agent proceeds without skill guidance.

signals.topic: `/desktop` command always fails on Windows with 'Failed to open Claude Desktop' even when Desktop app is fully installed and running
signals.summary: On Windows, the /desktop slash command always fails with 'Failed to open Claude Desktop. Please try opening it manually.' despite Claude Desktop being installed and running (10 processes visible, executable found at correct path). Workarounds (symlinks, CLAUDE_DESKTOP_PATH env var, reinstalling) all fail. /desktop is a key user-facing command.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocked: `/desktop` command (key user-facing feature) fails deterministically on Windows. Even manual workarounds (symlink, env var, fresh reinstall) don't resolve. Confirmed regression. The command is completely non-functional for Windows users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] /desktop fails on Windows - "Failed to open Claude Desktop" despite app being installed and running
source_issues.evidence: /desktop always fails on Windows 11. Claude Desktop installed and running (10 processes in Task Manager). Executable found at expected path. Tried symlink, CLAUDE_DESKTOP_PATH env var, multiple reinstalls — all fail identically. Explicitly confirmed as regression.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook notebook fails due to deprecated assistant message prefill API
signals.summary: The summarization cookbook notebook (capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb) raises a BadRequestError at cell 8 because it uses assistant message prefill, which is a deprecated API. The notebook's main execution path is blocked, preventing users from running the cookbook end-to-end.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime blocking bug: the cookbook's primary execution flow raises a BadRequestError due to a deprecated API (assistant message prefill). Users attempting to run the notebook end-to-end are immediately blocked at cell 8. While count=1 and single-repo scope prevents P0 classification, the blocking nature of the failure (main flow fails) qualifies it as a genuine user pain point warranting P1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: Cell 8 of the notebook raises BadRequestError: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' The full notebook execution path is blocked from this point onward.

signals.topic: Plugin submission pipeline shows 'Published' status but plugin never appears in marketplace.json — community plugins uninstallable
signals.summary: Community plugin submissions (llm-dark-patterns, sentry-error-assistant) report 'Published' in dashboard but never get added to marketplace.json, making them un-discoverable and uninstallable via the marketplace.
aliases: Plugin Published status does not mean marketplace inclusion
marketplace.json not updated after Published status
signals.review_reason: Two independent submitters hit the same pipeline gap: dashboard shows 'Published' but marketplace.json is never updated, so community plugins are undiscoverable. This is a core platform workflow failure that blocks the primary publish flow. Known regression from #1272 (closed without resolution), confirming systemic issue.

source_issues.title: Submission published but not appearing in marketplace.json: llm-dark-patterns (follow-up to #1272)
source_issues.evidence: Plugin shows 'Published' in dashboard at claude.ai/settings/plugins/submissions but verification of marketplace.json (1715 entries) shows zero matches. End-user impact: 'claude plugin install llm-dark-patterns@claude-community' does not resolve. Same root cause as closed-unresolved #1272.

source_issues.title: Plugin marked as 'Published' on submissions but not visible on claude.com/plugins
source_issues.evidence: Plugin 'sentry-error-assistant' shows 'Published' status but returns 'Nothing to see here' at claude.com/plugins/sentry-error-assistant and does not appear in plugin directory. No confirmation email received. Explicitly cites #1272 as same pattern.

signals.topic: skill-creator description optimizer completely non-functional on Windows — 5 distinct bugs cause 100% failure rate
signals.summary: The skill-creator plugin's quantitative description-optimization loop (run_loop.py, run_eval.py) is completely broken on Windows due to multiple POSIX-only assumptions: subprocess path resolution, select() on pipes, encoding defaults, and a recall=0% trigger-detection failure even after all other bugs are patched.
aliases: skill-creator description optimizer broken on Windows
Windows POSIX compatibility in skill-creator scripts
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports with combined 5+ distinct bugs all causing 100% failure of the description optimizer on Windows. #1850 explicitly confirms recall=0% even after all compat bugs are patched, meaning the core feature is completely broken for all Windows users. The skill creation quality-assurance loop is the plugin's primary value proposition.

source_issues.title: skill-creator description optimizer (run_loop.py) unusable on Windows — 4+ POSIX-only assumptions
source_issues.evidence: Documents 4 independent bugs: (1) subprocess can't find 'claude.CMD' on Windows, (2) select.select() only works on sockets on Windows not pipes, (3) read_text/write_text defaults to cp1252 causing Mojibake and UnicodeEncodeError, (4) subprocess.run text=True encodes stdin with cp1252. After patching all 4, loop still exits 1 (5th unisolated issue).

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop.py / run_eval.py description optimizer is non-functional on Windows (5 distinct bugs + recall=0% even after compat patches)
source_issues.evidence: Confirms 5 distinct bugs: (1-5 same as #1875). Key finding: even after patching all 5 bugs, the trigger-detection mechanism still returns precision=100%/recall=0% — the temp .claude/commands/ files are not reaching the spawned claude -p subprocess's available_skills list. Absolute 100% failure of the core feature.

signals.topic: session-report and security-guidance hardcode ~/.claude/ — break for users with custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
signals.summary: Both session-report and security-guidance plugins hardcode the config directory path (~/.claude/) instead of respecting the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable. Users with custom config directories get broken lookups and state files written to the wrong location.
signals.review_reason: Two plugins independently fail to respect the documented CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable, causing broken behavior for any user with a custom config directory. This is a configuration gap, not a crash, and both are fixable with a one-line env-var check. Prioritized as P2 due to count=2 and non-blocking nature.

source_issues.title: session-report: hardcodes ~/.claude/projects — must support CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
source_issues.evidence: analyze-sessions.mjs hardcodes path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude', 'projects') for transcript root. When CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set to a non-default location, session-report looks in the wrong place and finds no sessions.

source_issues.title: security-guidance: hardcodes ~/.claude/ — must respect CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
source_issues.evidence: security_reminder_hook.py lines 131 and 137 hardcode ~/.claude/ for state files instead of checking CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Security warning state files are written to the wrong location, breaking state persistence.

signals.topic: Discord plugin exits prematurely on stdin EOF before gateway login completes — bot never connects
signals.summary: The Discord plugin's shutdown handler is bound to stdin 'end'/'close' events which fire immediately after MCP handshake, before the async gateway WebSocket login completes. The process exits before the bot ever comes online.
aliases: Discord plugin gateway login race condition
signals.review_reason: Discord plugin is completely non-functional for any user on any platform due to a race condition between MCP stdio bridge EOF and async gateway login. The plugin process exits before the bot is ever online. This is a hard startup failure, not a degraded state.

source_issues.title: discord channel plugin: stdin EOF triggers shutdown before gateway login completes
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: server.ts binds shutdown() to process.stdin 'end' and 'close', which fire within milliseconds of MCP initialize handshake completing — before client.login(TOKEN) finishes the gateway WebSocket handshake. Plugin process exits via process.exit(0) before client.once('ready') can fire. Discord bot stays offline entirely. Demonstrated with code reference at lines 735-736.

signals.topic: huggingface-skills .mcp.json fails Zod schema validation — 100-line error dump on every plugin reload
signals.summary: The huggingface-skills plugin ships an .mcp.json with a bare {url: string} config that doesn't match any of Claude Code's 8 MCP server-config schema variants, causing a ~100-line Zod union error on every plugin reload.
aliases: huggingface-skills MCP config schema validation failure
Zod validation error on huggingface-skills plugin load
signals.review_reason: Plugin loads a broken .mcp.json that fails schema validation on every reload, producing a ~100-line error dump. This causes a degraded/critical experience for every user of the huggingface-skills plugin. While it may not hard-block all functionality, the repeated error dump is a severe UX failure that indicates the plugin's MCP server is misconfigured.

source_issues.title: huggingface-skills 1.0.1: invalid .mcp.json bare-url config fails Zod validation in Claude Code 2.1.x
source_issues.evidence: Plugin ships {mcpServers: {huggingface-skills: {url: 'https://huggingface.co/mcp?login'}}} which lacks the required 'type' field. Fails Zod validation producing ~100-line error dump on every plugin reload. Fix requires adding 'type: streamable-http'. Affects all users of huggingface-skills plugin.

signals.topic: README 中的文档链接失效（404），导致用户无法访问 Browser Tools API Demo 快速入门页面
signals.summary: README.md 中指向 browser-tools-api-demo 的链接返回 404，用户点击后无法访问该快速入门资源，影响新用户上手体验。
signals.review_reason: 该问题有明确用户影响证据：用户在尝试访问 Browser Tools API Demo 快速入门时遭遇 404，导致学习路径断裂，属于用户体验下降类痛点。但因仅涉及单条链接且 count=1，不满足 P0 高频阻断标准，归为 P2。排除纯功能请求和路线图讨论，确认为有效用户痛点。

source_issues.title: Documentation: Broken link in README
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 README.md 中点击指向 browser-tools-api-demo 的链接，收到 404 错误，无法访问该快速入门内容。3 条评论说明该问题被多人确认。

signals.topic: Tools API output chunking limitation causes 400 errors and blocks scalable long-form content generation
signals.summary: Users leveraging the Tools API for streaming/chunked long outputs encounter API validation errors (400 invalid_request_error) when tool_result blocks are provided without preceding tool_use blocks, and cannot scale due to context window accumulation requirements.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user workflow blocker. The issue explicitly documents a 400 API validation error that prevents the user from completing their core task (generating long-form human rights complaint documents via chunked tool calls). The user describes two compounding problems: (1) the API rejects properly structured tool_result blocks due to unclear sequencing requirements, and (2) the workaround (resending full context) does not scale beyond 200k tokens. While only 1 issue is present in this dataset, the evidence is strong — explicit error code, blocked primary workflow, and a feature usage question with no clear documentation answer.

source_issues.title: ToolUse: How to use tools to scalably chunk output beyond output token limit?
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly receives 400 error: "messages.0: `tool_result` block(s) provided when previous message does not contain any `tool_use` blocks". User describes being blocked from building a scalable document summarization pipeline, and is forced to send entire conversation history back to the API which consumes the 200k context window rapidly. No clear guidance exists on correct sequential tool_use/tool_result block ordering for multi-chunk output scenarios.

signals.topic: No native mechanism to share skills across a team — ~/.claude/skills/ is per-machine, forcing manual sync or third-party workarounds
signals.summary: Users building skills for team use have no official way to distribute them. Each teammate must manually sync, leading to drift, onboarding friction, and wasted effort on workaround solutions.
signals.review_reason: Multiple users across separate issues report being blocked from effectively using skills as a team. The workaround burden is real — users built third-party tools and tried multiple sync strategies before giving up. This is a clear adoption blocker for team environments, even though it's not a code crash.

source_issues.title: Enable org-wide skill sharing in Claude.ai
source_issues.evidence: Users must download .skill files and send via Slack/Teams, colleagues then manually upload via Settings > Capabilities. 13 comments from multiple users corroborating the pain. Open since Jan 2026.

source_issues.title: docs: any guidance on sharing SKILL.md across a team?
source_issues.evidence: Per-machine ~/.claude/skills/ means adding a new skill requires every team member to re-sync manually. User's team tried git submodule, dotfiles sync, and self-hosted registry — ended up building a third-party tool (skillnote). 5 engineers affected.

signals.topic: skill-creator run_loop.py crashes between iterations when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set, blocking the optimization workflow for subscription-only users
signals.summary: skill-creator's improve step directly constructs Anthropic() client requiring ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, while the eval step uses claude -p via user subscription — causing a crash mid-loop for users without an API key.
aliases: run_loop.py authentication mismatch subscription vs API key
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is broken with full repro steps. The optimization loop crashes mid-iteration for any user running on a Claude/Claude Code subscription without an API key. The eval step works but the improve step blocks — meaning the user wastes time on iteration 1 before hitting a hard crash. This is a primary use path of the skill-creator skill, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop.py improve step crashes without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (inconsistent with eval step)
source_issues.evidence: Iteration 1 completes via claude -p (user subscription) but crashes at improve_description.py:114 when calling client.messages.create(...) with TypeError about missing auth. Full repro steps provided.

signals.topic: Shared skills expose full instruction content — no option to share capability without revealing proprietary prompting logic
signals.summary: Organizations wanting to share skills with colleagues or within an org have no way to protect the underlying instructions, limiting skills adoption in competitive or IP-sensitive environments.
aliases: skills cannot hide instructions when shared
signals.review_reason: This is a feature gap that materially blocks organizational adoption of skills — if proprietary prompting logic must be exposed to share the capability, teams with IP concerns simply cannot use the sharing feature. Count is 1 so P2 is appropriate; it does not meet the P0 bar without corroboration across multiple users.

source_issues.title: Feature Request: Skill sharing with hidden instructions
source_issues.evidence: Recipients of shared skills can preview full contents and copy instructions into their own skills. Organizations with proprietary workflows have no path to share capabilities without exposing underlying logic. Explicitly blocks organizational adoption.

signals.topic: DeepSeek v4-pro reasoning mode: multi-turn tool calls fail with HTTP 400 'reasoning_content must be passed back'
signals.summary: When using deepseek-v4-pro with thinking mode enabled, any conversation involving a tool call fails with a hard 400 error on the turn where the tool result is returned to the model. Goose strips `reasoning_content` from assistant messages when constructing the next API request, but DeepSeek's thinking-mode API requires this field to be preserved verbatim. No workaround exists without disabling reasoning or tool calls entirely.
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn agentic tool use is completely broken for deepseek-v4-pro with thinking mode. Hard 400 error with no workaround other than disabling the core capability. Blocks production use of agentic workflows with this model.

source_issues.title: deepseek-v4-pro (thinking mode): multi-turn tool calls fail with 400 'reasoning_content must be passed back to the API'
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 error on first tool result turn. Root cause same as #7363. Users must disable reasoning mode or not use tool calling, both defeating the purpose of agentic runtime. 2 comments, closed.

source_issues.title: Incompatible with DeepSeek v4-pro
source_issues.evidence: Generic report of incompatibility; DeepSeek v4-pro returns reasoning_content field that other models do not. Closed without resolution details.

signals.topic: Linux binary breakage on older distros: v1.34.0 requires glibc 2.38, breaking Ubuntu 22.04 LTS/Debian 12/RHEL
signals.summary: After build infrastructure was migrated to Ubuntu 24.04, the published v1.34.0 Linux binary links against glibc 2.38/2.39 and fails to start on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35), Debian 12, and RHEL 8/9 with a clear version error. This is a silent breaking change affecting all Linux users on stable LTS distributions.
signals.review_reason: Binary fails to start entirely on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and other stable Linux distros. Clear blocking error at startup. No workaround except downgrading. Directly caused by v1.34.0 build infrastructure change.

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 requires libc6 2.38
source_issues.evidence: Binary fails to start on Ubuntu 22.04 with 'GLIBC_2.38 not found' error. Build changed to Ubuntu 24.04 runners in #9075. Breaks Debian 12 and RHEL 8/9 as well. Downgrading to v1.33.1 fixes it.

signals.topic: v1.34.0 Linux binary silently requires libvulkan.so.1 at startup, not documented in release notes
signals.summary: The Vulkan feature was compiled into the published Linux tarball by default (not truly opt-in as documented), adding a new runtime dependency on libvulkan.so.1 that was absent in v1.33.x. Users who run cloud-provider inference (e.g. AWS Bedrock) and never use local inference are still blocked by the missing library at startup.
signals.review_reason: Binary fails to start due to undocumented new runtime dependency, even for users on the cloud-only inference path. Silent breaking change with no entry in release notes or breaking changes section.

source_issues.title: v1.34.0 published Linux binary requires libvulkan.so.1 at startup — not flagged in release notes
source_issues.evidence: Binary fails with 'error while loading shared libraries: libvulkan.so.1' on systems without Vulkan loader. Affects users using only cloud inference (AWS Bedrock) who never touch local inference. No mention in v1.34.0 release notes or CHANGELOG. PR #9038 enabled vulkan in Linux CI/bundle paths, making it non-opt-in for published artifacts.

signals.topic: GCP location routing regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, silently breaking Gemini 3.x with zero tokens
signals.summary: known_location() introduced in #6393 hardcodes Iowa for all Gemini(_) variants. Gemini 3.x requires the global endpoint (404 on us-central1). The retry logic only fires when configured_location differs from known_location, so with default config (Iowa), the mismatch is never detected and requests silently hit 404 and exit with zero tokens. No error is surfaced, making the issue invisible.
signals.review_reason: Key Gemini 3.x models are silently broken with zero tokens and no error message, making the issue invisible to users. Affects all users with default GCP config who try Gemini 3.x models on Vertex AI. Workaround requires manual config change.

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed 404 on us-central1 vs 200 on global endpoint via direct API call. Session created, model set, but zero tokens generated with no error. Gemini 3.1-flash-lite-preview released March 2026 has been broken since #6393. Workaround of setting GCP_LOCATION=global is known but suboptimal. Closed after fix.

signals.topic: Windows: Browser not launching for authentication, blocking Copilot/Azure/other provider logins
signals.summary: On Windows (especially corporate-managed workstations), Goose fails to launch a browser window for authentication flows (GitHub Copilot, Azure, etc.) because it cannot resolve executable paths for browser and az CLI. The PATH resolution assumptions that work on Linux do not hold in Windows enterprise environments where software is installed in non-standard locations.
aliases: windows auth executables not in PATH
signals.review_reason: Authentication is completely blocked on Windows enterprise environments. Users cannot log in to critical providers (Copilot, Azure) making Goose unusable for their workflows. Reproducible with screenshot evidence.

source_issues.title: Windows: Browser not launching for authentication
source_issues.evidence: No browser window launches for auth. UI shows 'A browser window will open for you to complete the login' but nothing happens. Blocks Copilot, Azure and other auth-dependent providers. Screenshot attached showing the broken state. Affects enterprise Windows environments with restricted PATH.

signals.topic: FlowLogger AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith() causes runtime crash on Cloudflare Workers (v3.2.0+)
signals.summary: Stagehand v3.2.0+ crashes immediately on Cloudflare Workers because FlowLogger.init() calls AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith(), which Cloudflare Workers intentionally does not implement. This blocks any user attempting to run Stagehand on Cloudflare Workers before any browser interaction occurs.
aliases: AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith() not supported on Cloudflare Workers
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed runtime crash that blocks Stagehand from initializing entirely on Cloudflare Workers, a supported deployment target. The crash occurs at stagehand.init() before any browser interaction, making the library completely unusable on that runtime in v3.2.0+. The user was forced to implement a monkey-patch workaround, indicating significant user impact and a blocking regression introduced in v3.2.0.

source_issues.title: FlowLogger breaks on Cloudflare Workers: enterWith() is not supported
source_issues.evidence: stagehand.init() crashes immediately with 'asyncLocalStorage.enterWith() is not implemented' on Cloudflare Workers with v3.2.0+. Workaround requires monkey-patching AsyncLocalStorage.prototype.enterWith before importing Stagehand. Affects all users on v3.2.0+ running on Cloudflare Workers including browser automation via Browser Rendering binding.

signals.topic: TypeScript type checking fails with NodeNext module resolution due to missing ai/dist export entry
signals.summary: When using TypeScript with NodeNext module resolution and strict checks (noEmit), stagehand fails to build because it imports from 'ai/dist' which is not declared in the ai package's exports field, causing tsc to report type resolution errors.
aliases: tsc type check fails with nodenext module resolution
ai package missing dist export causing build failures
signals.review_reason: TypeScript type checking failures with NodeNext module resolution prevent developers from integrating Stagehand into TypeScript projects using strict module resolution settings, blocking the build pipeline. This is a packaging/release issue where the package's internal imports reference paths not exposed in the dependency's public exports, causing tsc failures. While not a runtime crash, it directly blocks development workflow for users with strict TypeScript configurations.

source_issues.title: Failed `tsc` types with full check
source_issues.evidence: Building the repo under tsconfig with NodeNext module resolution and tsc --noEmit causes the stagehand package to look for 'ai/dist' in the ai package exports, but 'ai/dist' is not exported from the ai package's exports field, resulting in a build-time type resolution failure. Repro requires strict TS config with nodenext module, rewriteRelativeImportExtensions, erasableSyntaxOnly, and verbatimModuleSyntax enabled.

signals.topic: Long conversation streaming causes UI stuttering and text rendering bursts
signals.summary: Long text or multi-turn conversations cause SSE streaming to render with visible stuttering, text appearing in bursts, and UI freezing. Multiple reports indicate this has been an ongoing issue across several releases.
signals.review_reason: 4条issue独立报告同一问题，且有详细SSE wire capture数据证明74.27%的响应体积为冗余数据，导致UI卡顿、文本突发出现。这是高频发生的主流程体验问题，用户在每次长对话时都能感知到显著体验下降。

source_issues.title: 一些影响用户使用体验的问题
source_issues.evidence: 长文本或多轮对话时，流式输出不够顺畅，文本会分段突发出现，UI也有卡顿感；issue中引用了#2972、#2981、#2396、#2785等多个历史issue确认此问题反复发生

source_issues.title: [Bug] UI Stream 流式渲染卡顿，长文本响应时界面不流畅
source_issues.evidence: 流式渲染不连贯，明显卡顿；流式输出期间UI间歇性冻结；文本以突发方式出现而非连续流式；CPU占用过高

source_issues.title: Reduce redundant SSE values payload in chat streams
source_issues.evidence: values事件占总SSE响应74.27%，其中99.86%为重复的历史消息；85.12%的消息字节是重复传输；移除后SSE体积减少75%

source_issues.title: Long conversation output performance degradation (cross-reference in #2995)
source_issues.evidence: 长对话场景下的流媒体性能问题（已在#2995中引用）

signals.topic: Historical messages cannot be loaded from current page after context compression
signals.summary: After context compression occurs in an active chat page, scrolling to the top does not trigger loading of earlier historical messages. Users can only see messages after the most recent compression. Reopening the same thread fixes it, indicating the data exists but the load trigger is broken.
aliases: 上下文压缩后历史丢失
signals.review_reason: 上下文压缩后早期消息在当前页面无法加载，用户失去对话历史的连续访问能力。两个issue从不同角度描述了同一问题的不同层面——前端加载触发失效和checkpoint恢复导致历史不可见。有明确的数据存在性证明（重新打开可加载），用户体验影响可复现。

source_issues.title: 新对话页发生上下文压缩后继续聊天，顶部无法继续加载更早历史消息
source_issues.evidence: 同一新对话页连续聊天触发上下文压缩后，页面顶部无法加载更早历史消息；但重新打开已有对话后可正常加载；证明数据存在于后端但前端加载触发失效

source_issues.title: 上下文压缩之后历史消息丢失
source_issues.evidence: PR #2153将/history接口数据从event store恢复成checkpoint后，前端界面不显示被压缩的消息；runs/{run_id}/messages接口目前无作用；历史消息对用户不可见

signals.topic: Search tool reports unavailable, causing multi-turn agent task to halt
signals.summary: When agents need to call the search tool, the system reports the tool is unavailable. Different LLMs (Qwen, DeepSeek) respond differently, but in all cases the agent fails to follow the prompt instruction to find alternatives or continue the task. This is a core workflow blocker.
signals.review_reason: 搜索工具不可用直接导致多轮agent任务完全阻断，用户无法完成依赖搜索的主流程任务。即使不同LLM有不同行为，结果都是工具未按prompt要求工作。issue中明确记录了具体prompt、系统行为差异和prompt指令未被执行的事实，具有明确用户影响证据。

source_issues.title: 一些影响用户使用体验的问题
source_issues.evidence: prompt明确说明需要调用搜索工具，但deerflow报告工具不可用；千问在报告工具不可用后停止输出，deepseek虽能继续但搜索工具本身不可用；prompt要求找不到工具时寻找替代方法但未被执行

signals.topic: skill_evolution blocked by security_scanner's strict JSON parsing — feature completely unusable
signals.summary: With skill_evolution.enabled, legitimate skill writes are silently blocked. The security_scanner requires raw JSON from moderation LLMs, but modern LLMs (GPT-5.x, Claude, etc.) frequently wrap output in markdown fences or reasoning prose, causing the parser to fail and fall back to conservative 'block'. skill_evolution is effectively unusable in default configurations.
signals.review_reason: 虽然涉及安全扫描器，但核心用户影响是skill_evolution功能完全不可用——用户启用功能后，任何合法的skill写入都被静默阻止，并附带误导性错误信息。HTTP 200日志证明moderation模型实际正常工作，问题在于parser过于严格。有完整日志证据和精确根因分析，用户影响明确。

source_issues.title: Skill security_scanner blocks legitimate skill_evolution writes due to overly strict JSON parsing of LLM moderation output
source_issues.evidence: skill_evolution.enabled=true时，moderation LLM返回HTTP 200但写入仍被阻止；错误信息为'Security scan unavailable for skill content'但模型实际已响应；问题是parser无法处理代码围栏格式；skill_evolution对大多数主流LLM用户完全不可用

signals.topic: Historical run records disappear after gateway service restart
signals.summary: After configuring PostgreSQL persistence and restarting the gateway, the /api/threads/{thread_id}/runs endpoint returns an empty list even though records exist in the database. Users lose access to their conversation run history.
signals.review_reason: 服务重启后用户完全无法查询历史运行记录，核心功能数据丢失。配置了PostgreSQL持久化但数据仍不可访问，属于主流程阻断性问题。issue中明确指出数据库中数据存在但接口返回空列表，用户影响证据直接。

source_issues.title: 服务重启后 /api/threads/{thread_id}/runs 接口无法查询到历史运行记录
source_issues.evidence: 配置PostgreSQL持久化后，重启gateway服务导致/api/threads/{thread_id}/runs接口返回空列表，但数据库中确实存在该thread的历史run记录；用户完全丢失对话历史访问能力

signals.topic: CLI 'Unknown or disabled provider openai' error blocks all OpenAI-compatible endpoint users — works in VS Code but fails in CLI
signals.summary: When configuring an OpenAI-compatible endpoint via CLI TUI, users get 'Error: Unknown or disabled provider openai' and cannot use the feature. 15+ comments indicate widespread impact. The same configuration works in VS Code extension.
aliases: openai compatible provider not recognized CLI
Unknown or disabled provider openai CLI
signals.review_reason: Three distinct issues converge on the same root cause: CLI fails to properly configure/recognize OpenAI-compatible providers while VS Code extension succeeds. High comment count (15+) on #10750 confirms widespread user impact. Users cannot use their own LLM endpoints in CLI.

source_issues.title: Error: Unknown or disabled provider "openai".
source_issues.evidence: CLI TUI setup flow for OpenAI Compatible endpoint results in 'Unknown or disabled provider openai' error. 15 comments indicating widespread user impact.

source_issues.title: How to disable auto-update in Cline CLI? Multiple issues with v2.18.0
source_issues.evidence: After auto-update, OpenAI-compatible API provider fails with 'Unknown or disabled provider openai' error — same error as #10750.

source_issues.title: Error: self signed certificate in certificate chain
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI Compatible endpoint with self-signed certificate fails. Affects vLLM OpenAI endpoint users in CLI.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock profile authentication completely broken in CLI 3.0.2 — region and profile options not passed to AI SDK
signals.summary: CLI 3.0.2 fails to authenticate with AWS Bedrock when using profile-based credentials. Root cause identified: options field missing from GatewayProviderConfig in handler-factory.ts, so region, profile, and credentials are never forwarded to @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock. Same config works in VS Code extension.
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports with detailed root cause analysis. All confirm the same regression: CLI 3.0.2 completely blocks AWS Bedrock profile users. Explicitly identified code location (handler-factory.ts lines 101-114). Multiple users confirmed downgrade to 2.18.0 resolves the issue, confirming this is a regression.

source_issues.title: AWS Bedrock profile authentication broken in CLI 3.0.2
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis provided: options field missing from GatewayProviderConfig. AWS region/profile/credentials never forwarded to AI SDK. VS Code extension works because it uses different code path.

source_issues.title: Allow other AWS Bedrock connection methods in latest CLI version not only API Key
source_issues.evidence: AWS profile authentication not working in CLI 3.0.2. 'Use existing configuration' doesn't list models. Returns 403 when typing model ID.

source_issues.title: Error: AWS region setting is missing. Pass it using the 'region' parameter or the AWS_REGION environment variable.
source_issues.evidence: CLI 3.0.2 breaks AWS Bedrock profile auth. Error appears immediately on any prompt. Same config works in 2.18.0 (regression). 6 comments confirming widespread impact.

signals.topic: Multiple third-party providers fail in VS Code: MiniMax auth error, Cerebras unsupported parameters, Together AI model list missing
signals.summary: MiniMax provider returns 401 authentication error with valid API key, Cerebras provider rejects tool calls with unsupported 'effort' and 'reasoningSummary' fields, Together AI provider fails to load model list. All three provider integrations are broken for VS Code users.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct third-party providers are simultaneously broken in VS Code. While each is a separate provider issue, the pattern of provider integration failures indicates systemic QA gaps. Users choosing alternatives to primary providers are blocked.

source_issues.title: [Windows specific] MiniMax AI Provider: invalid x-api-key is shown when trying to use any minimax LLM
source_issues.evidence: MiniMax provider returns 401 'invalid x-api-key' error with a valid API key on Windows. Users cannot use MiniMax provider.

source_issues.title: Cerebras Provider: effort and reasoningSummary unsupported error with zai-glm-4.7 and gpt-oss-120b LLM
source_issues.evidence: Cerebras provider returns 'effort: property unsupported' and 'reasoningSummary: property unsupported' errors. Users cannot use zai-glm-4.7 or gpt-oss-120b models.

source_issues.title: Together AI Provider: List of Model is missing for together AI
source_issues.evidence: Together AI provider shows empty model list. Users cannot select a model to use with Together AI provider.

signals.topic: run_commands tool call schema validation failures cause task interruption across multiple LLM providers
signals.summary: run_commands tool calls are repeatedly rejected due to schema mismatches: GPT-5.5 emits unsupported 'timeout' field, DeepSeek API expects string/array field type mismatch. Tasks get stuck in thinking state and workflow is interrupted.
signals.review_reason: Tool call validation failures are actively blocking task execution. Users report tasks stuck in thinking state with explicit error messages. The first attempt consistently fails and the model must self-correct, causing measurable workflow interruption.

source_issues.title: Cline: Run_commands tool call failed intermittently for DeepSeek and task stuck in thinking state
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek provider: run_commands tool call fails with type validation error 'expected string, received array/object'. Task stuck in thinking state.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.2 with GPT-5.5 emits invalid run_commands tool calls containing unsupported timeout field
source_issues.evidence: GPT-5.5 emits run_commands with timeout:120000 field which is rejected as unrecognized key. Task workflow interrupted. Model retries without timeout to succeed.

signals.topic: CLI approval bypass: Reject button click does not prevent Cline from retrying and executing command
signals.summary: When user clicks 'Reject' on a pending command approval, Cline retries the command without asking for approval again and executes it, bypassing user intent. This is a security/correctness issue where the approval mechanism is ineffective.
signals.review_reason: User approval mechanism is actively bypassed — clicking Reject does not prevent execution. This is a core security control failure, not merely a UX issue. The approval dialog is rendered ineffective.

source_issues.title: Cline disregards required approval
source_issues.evidence: User clicks Reject button on a pending command, Cline retries the command without asking for approval again and executes it. Screenshot shows the Reject button click being bypassed.

signals.topic: Hardcoded shell invocations break terminal command execution for PowerShell Core (pwsh) and non-POSIX shells
signals.summary: Continue hardcodes `powershell.exe` and `-l` flags across the codebase, causing runtime failures for users on PowerShell Core 7+ and tcsh/csh shells. Failures are silent, unpredictable, and uncorrectable by end users.
signals.review_reason: Two hardcoded shell-invocation bugs (hardcoded powershell.exe + hardcoded -l flag) block terminal command execution for non-standard shell environments. count=2, both have clear reproduction steps and evidence of runtime failure. Combined they affect both Windows PowerShell Core users and tcsh users, covering the two most common non-POSIX shell environments.

source_issues.title: Hardcoded legacy Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe) causes runtime failures and degraded UX
source_issues.evidence: Script with ternary operator fails with 'Unexpected token ?' because powershell.exe cannot parse modern PowerShell Core syntax. Unicode strings silently corrupt (replaced with '?'). Uncorrectable by end users as invocation is hardcoded in app logic.

source_issues.title: Terminal commands fail when $SHELL is set to tcsh due to hardcoded -l shell flag
source_issues.evidence: tcsh does not support '-l' flag. Every terminal command fails with 'Unknown option: -l'. Reproducible on any Linux system with $SHELL=/bin/tcsh.

signals.topic: Markdown prompt files silently dropped during config load due to incorrect rule-type inference
signals.summary: Markdown files referenced via `uses: file://` in the `prompts` section are incorrectly parsed as Rules, wrapped in a `rules` key instead of `prompts`, and silently discarded. Users see no errors, and their prompt content is simply missing.
signals.review_reason: Single-issue but critical: markdown prompt files are silently discarded (no error shown), meaning user-defined prompt content never applies to sessions. The bug is confirmed with debug logs and root cause traced to unroll.ts. The silent failure pattern is especially harmful as users have no indication their configuration is incomplete.

source_issues.title: Markdown Files in prompts Section are Misidentified as Rules and Dropped
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in unroll.ts parseYamlOrMarkdownRule. Debug logs show 'WARNING - Section prompts not found in resolved block config'. The prompt file is read successfully (214 bytes) but silently dropped. Verified with --verbose logging. Proposed fix has been implemented.

signals.topic: Autocomplete produces truncated/wrong suggestions on large files due to incorrect prefix-suffix context calculation
signals.summary: On files over ~3000 lines, autocomplete returns wrong suggestions because the cursor position-based prefix and suffix are incorrectly computed. The same wrong suggestion persists regardless of cursor position. Affects JetBrains IDEs.
signals.review_reason: Core autocomplete feature is broken for large files on JetBrains IDEs (the second-most popular IDE after VS Code). User supplied paired log files proving the bug, and noted the same config works on VS Code, isolating it to JetBrains-specific code. The symptom (wrong suggestions persisting at any cursor position) indicates a fundamental calculation error.

source_issues.title: Truncated / wrong prefix & suffix on large file Autocompletion
source_issues.evidence: User provided prompt_correct.log and prompt_wrong.log showing identical wrong prefix/suffix regardless of cursor position on files >3000 lines. JetBrains IDE specifically affected; same config works on VS Code. Config uses contextLength=128000 but prefix/suffix calculation is clearly broken.

signals.topic: PR checks reuse stale session IDs on subsequent commits instead of creating fresh evaluations, causing misleading CI feedback
signals.summary: On pull_request.synchronize events, Continue re-posts GitHub commit statuses with the original task IDs from PR-open instead of creating fresh check sessions. CI statuses appear live but are stale results from old diffs, consuming significant developer debugging time.
aliases: PR checks not re-evaluating on updates
check sessions not invalidated on new commits
signals.review_reason: CI check staleness is a critical workflow issue: check statuses appear authoritative but are misleading, causing developers to waste hours. The user provided exhaustive evidence including raw API responses, task IDs, and status history timestamps. The bug is confirmed as server-side session management failure (sessions keyed by PR+check name, not by head SHA).

source_issues.title: PR checks do not create fresh agent sessions on PR updates; stale task IDs re-post to new commits
source_issues.evidence: 6 PR commits received the same 3 task IDs created at PR-open. Agents API confirmed only 3 sessions total despite 5 subsequent synchronize events. User spent ~6 hours debugging before identifying stale status. diff=null confirmed via API. The `cn checks` CLI also fails silently (exit 0, no output) removing the normal dismissal path.

signals.topic: Continue Hub login/authentication flow fails silently, leaving users unable to authenticate
signals.summary: Users cannot log in to Continue Hub via any login method. After completing the auth flow, the page redirects back to login and direct access to hub.continue.dev shows 'Not authenticated (user missing)'. Affects Windows users across both Edge and Chrome.
signals.review_reason: Authentication failure blocks users from accessing Continue Hub entirely, a core product surface. Multiple auth methods and workarounds all fail, with clear error messages from the hub itself. Recent issue (same day as data snapshot) indicating active impact.

source_issues.title: Login failed with "Not authenticated (user missing)" after account setup
source_issues.evidence: User tried multiple workarounds: clean browser profile, different login methods, cleared cookies/cache, revoked and re-granted GitHub OAuth. Both Edge and Chrome fail identically. VPN and network changes have no effect. Direct hub.continue.dev/inbox access shows 'Not authenticated (user missing)'.

signals.topic: ValkeyStorage metadata_filter references fields not defined in FT index schema — returns wrong results or errors
signals.summary: The `metadata_filter` clauses constructed in `ValkeyStorage._vector_search()` reference arbitrary metadata key fields (e.g. `@key:value`), but the `memory_index` FT schema only defines VectorField, TagField(scope, categories), and NumericField(created_at, importance). User-supplied metadata fields are not indexed, causing FT.SEARCH to error or silently return wrong results.
aliases: metadata_filter fields not indexed in memory_index FT schema (ValkeyStorage)
signals.review_reason: This is a functional bug where metadata_filter silently fails or errors when using ValkeyStorage. Both issues are identical duplicates, bringing count to 2. The issue clearly describes that user metadata fields are not in the FT index, causing FT.SEARCH to fail or return wrong results. This breaks a core memory filtering use case — users cannot filter Valkey-backed memory by custom metadata fields. Non-blocking because the storage layer may still return some results (via fallback), but results are unreliable.

source_issues.title: feat(valkey): metadata_filter fields not indexed in memory_index FT schema
source_issues.evidence: Both issues are identical duplicates filed by coderabbitai[bot] as part of PR #5703 review. Issue explicitly states metadata_filter will 'either error or silently return wrong results.' Raises two remediation options (materialize into FT index vs. post-filter). Affects any user trying to filter Valkey-backed memory by custom metadata.

source_issues.title: feat(valkey): metadata_filter fields not indexed in memory_index FT schema
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of issue #5795, same evidence.

signals.topic: Task retry triggers duplicate tool executions causing real financial/communication side effects
signals.summary: When a CrewAI task fails and is retried (via max_retry_limit, exception handling, or external re-trigger), any @tool decorated function that already executed runs again. No idempotency guard exists. This can cause duplicate payments, emails, trades, or other irreversible external API calls. The issue was independently confirmed via LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 showing the same failure pattern in production.
aliases: Tool re-execution on retry has no idempotency guard
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed P0 workflow runtime bug with clear user-impact evidence: duplicate side effects (payments, emails, trades) on task retry. Marked 'bug', 17 comments indicating community concern. Referenced LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 showing same production failure pattern. This blocks any crew using @tool with external API calls — a core production use case. High severity due to financial/irreversible consequences.

source_issues.title: Tool re-execution on task retry has no idempotency guard — duplicate payments, emails, trades possible
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with explicit reproduction steps: @tool with external API call (payment/email) fires twice on retry. 17 comments, high community interest. Cross-referenced with LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 confirming same failure pattern in production. In-memory dedup doesn't survive worker re-dispatch. Fix requires durable external storage keyed before execution starts.

signals.topic: Knowledge metadata filtering not exposed through KnowledgeConfig or Agent — users cannot filter memory by metadata despite storage layer support
signals.summary: The storage layer (KnowledgeStorage.search with metadata_filter, BaseRecord, BaseKnowledgeSource) fully supports metadata, but the user-facing API is broken: KnowledgeConfig has no metadata_filter field, Knowledge.query()/aquery() silently drops metadata_filter, Crew.query_knowledge() lacks the parameter, and BaseKnowledgeSource.self.metadata is never written to stored documents. Users of Qdrant (and Valkey) cannot filter their knowledge base by custom metadata.
aliases: Knowledge metadata filtering not configurable via KnowledgeConfig / Agent
Knowledge metadata_filter silently dropped in query pipeline
signals.review_reason: This is a real functional gap: the underlying storage supports metadata filtering but the user-facing API is broken at 4 distinct points in the pipeline. While labeled 'feature-request', it describes a regression-like behavior where features that should work (metadata filtering in knowledge base) are completely inaccessible to users. The 4 identified gaps are specific and verifiable. This blocks users who need metadata-filtered knowledge retrieval — a legitimate production use case.

source_issues.title: Knowledge metadata supported in storage but not configurable via KnowledgeConfig / Agent
source_issues.evidence: Detailed technical bug describing 4 gaps: (1) KnowledgeConfig has no metadata_filter field, (2) Knowledge.query()/aquery() silently drops metadata_filter, (3) Crew.query_knowledge() has no metadata_filter param, (4) BaseKnowledgeSource.self.metadata is never written to vector store documents. 3 comments indicating active community discussion. Author uses Qdrant in production and needs this for metadata-based retrieval in agentic pipelines.

signals.topic: OAuth/Auth login failures blocking CLI usage entirely
signals.summary: Users across multiple environments (Linux, macOS, Windows) cannot authenticate via Sign in with Google, causing endless login loops or OAuth failures. Affects both free and paid personal accounts.
signals.review_reason: Four distinct auth failures all resulting in users being unable to use the CLI at all. Multiple distinct root causes (seatbelt profile, account entitlement mapping, token exchange, untrusted folder env loading) but same user impact: CLI is completely unusable after auth attempt. Count=4 >= 3, affects core login workflow.

source_issues.title: Google OAuth login for personal accounts may not be reliably mapped to the correct entitlement path in Gemini CLI
source_issues.evidence: Personal Google accounts get API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED at googleapis.com edge gateway after OAuth succeeds; user describes endless 'crying' loop. Client-side post-auth runtime path depends entirely on backend tier response with no explicit account type branching.

source_issues.title: Bug: OAuth Not Authorized Error during Sign in with Google (v0.42.0)
source_issues.evidence: Fresh install: OAuth completes in browser but redirected to 'Sign in failed' with 'products not yet authorized' error. Token exchange then fails. CLI session drops entirely.

source_issues.title: [macOS] strict-open seatbelt profile blocks OAuth authentication flow
source_issues.evidence: strict-open seatbelt profile causes OAuth authentication to fail silently, rendering CLI unusable in sandbox mode. Switching to permissive-open allows auth to proceed.

source_issues.title: ~/.gemini/.env VS untrusted folder
source_issues.evidence: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set in ~/.gemini/.env works in trusted folders but causes 'invalid credentials' and endless login loop in untrusted folders. Workspace users forced to set env var globally.

signals.topic: Shell execution memory/FD leaks causing PTY exhaustion and ENXIO errors in long-lived sessions
signals.summary: PTY processes and scrollback buffers are never garbage collected when log stream end() callback fails, causing memory leak and file descriptor exhaustion. Root cause of ENXIO errors in long-running CLI sessions.
signals.review_reason: Two separate but related shell execution failures: (1) PTY leak causing permanent memory/FD exhaustion in long-lived sessions, explicitly documented as root cause of ENXIO errors; (2) non-atomic security policy causing partial command execution and deadlock. Both are main-flow blocking — shell execution is a core CLI workflow.

source_issues.title: PTY memory and file descriptor leak in ShellExecutionService
source_issues.evidence: Memory and FD leak: activePtys.delete wrapped in Promise.then of cleanupLogStream; if stream fails to emit end(), Promise hangs indefinitely, leaving PTY and scrollback buffer in memory permanently. Root cause of ENXIO errors when PTY exhaustion occurs.

source_issues.title: Non-atomic policy enforcement and synchronous I/O deadlock during command chaining
source_issues.evidence: Security policy partially executes first command of a chain before blocking the remainder, leaving filesystem in inconsistent state. CLI then hangs on obscured synchronous confirmation prompt requiring SIGINT to recover.

signals.topic: Crash on startup or unhandled promise rejection crashes in specific environments
signals.summary: CLI crashes on startup with fatal errors in Termux (Android) and when chat history contains subdirectories, causing crash loops especially in containerized environments.
signals.review_reason: Two crash-on-startup scenarios: (1) ENAMETOOLONG on Termux causing unhandled promise rejection crash; (2) EISDIR from chat history scan when subdirectories created. Both cause fatal CLI crashes, with the latter creating infinite restart loops in containers. Count=2 with severe user impact (CLI completely unusable).

source_issues.title: Error
source_issues.evidence: Unhandled Promise Rejection: ENAMETOOLONG error crashes CLI on Termux (Android). Critical error shown to user with stack trace. State: closed.

source_issues.title: Crash Loop due to /chat save <tag> creating subdirectories.
source_issues.evidence: /chat save with spaces creates subdirectory in tmp/. On restart, history-loading logic reads it as a file triggering EISDIR (illegal operation on directory), causing fatal crash. In containerized environments (Home Assistant) this creates infinite restart loop.

signals.topic: Bundled proxy-agent dynamic import exposes non-constructor causing HttpsProxyAgent errors in enterprise proxy environments
signals.summary: After PR #26361, the bundled fallback path for https-proxy-agent still fails with 'HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor' due to esbuild ESM/CJS interop issue. Only affects bundled CLI with proxy configured, not dev mode.
signals.review_reason: Clear functional failure in enterprise proxy environments: CLI throws uncaught TypeError and fails to make API calls when proxy is configured. Not all users affected, but for those in proxy setups (common in enterprises) the CLI is completely non-functional in bundled form while working from source.

source_issues.title: Bundled proxy-agent fallback can still fail with 'HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor' after #26361
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent3 is not a constructor in bundled CLI with Vertex AI auth + external-account credentials + HTTPS_PROXY configured. Root cause: esbuild splits HttpsProxyAgent under .default.HttpsProxyAgent but gaxios looks for named .HttpsProxyAgent export. Running from source with npm run start does not reproduce.

signals.topic: UTF-8 shell command output garbling on Windows with non-UTF8 ANSI code pages (CP936/GBK)
signals.summary: On Windows with non-UTF8 system locale (e.g., CP936/GBK Chinese), run_shell_command output is double-decoded producing mojibake, corrupting AI context and user-visible terminal output.
signals.review_reason: Shell command output is completely unreliable for Windows users with non-UTF8 locales — a large international user base. The output corruption propagates to AI context causing hallucination and task failure, and users must avoid the core run_shell_command tool entirely.

source_issues.title: run_shell_command continuously garbles UTF-8 stdout on systems with non-UTF8 ANSI code pages (e.g., CP936)
source_issues.evidence: Windows with Chinese locale (CP936/GBK): Node captures stdout bytes and decodes using system ANSI code page instead of UTF-8. Results in severely garbled mojibake passed to LLM context and printed to terminal. Root cause: shell wrapper uses powershell.exe without forcing UTF-8 encoding. Users forced to avoid run_shell_command for file reading.

signals.topic: Windows 用户无法通过 uv 安装 smolagents[dev]：mlx[cpu] 无 Windows 兼容 wheel
