source_issues.title: BUG:  No solution found when resolving dependencies while uv
source_issues.evidence: Windows 用户分别在 Python 3.11 和 3.12 环境下使用 uv 安装 smolagents[dev]，均因 mlx[cpu] 无 win_amd64 wheel 而安装失败，主流程完全阻断

signals.topic: ToolSerializer.dumps f-string 转义错误导致序列化失败时错误信息无意义
signals.summary: serialization.py 第 429 行使用双花括号 {{e}} 输出字面量字符串 {e}，而非插值异常对象。当 pickle 序列化失败时，用户看到的错误信息是 'Cannot serialize object: {e}' 而非真实异常内容，无法定位问题。
aliases: f-string escape bug serialization error message
pickle serialization error hides real exception
signals.review_reason: 当用户序列化自定义对象失败时，看到的是 '{e}' 字面量而非真实异常原因，属于关键功能（序列化/反序列化）产生误导性错误消息，显著降低调试效率。同文件内对比明显（line 292 正确），是确认的 bug。count=1 故 P2。

source_issues.title: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message
source_issues.evidence: 代码使用 f"{{e}}" 输出字面量 {e}，正确写法应为 f"{e}"；同一文件第 292 行使用了正确写法。对比明显——序列化失败时用户完全看不到真实异常，调试受阻。

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware 处理空 LLM 响应时崩溃（IndexError）或静默返回空结果，阻断父agent获取子agent结果
signals.summary: SubAgentMiddleware 在 _run_subagent 中访问 result['messages'][-1] 时，若 LLM 返回空消息列表则抛出 IndexError；若 LLM 在 tool call 后返回空 AIMessage 则静默向父agent传递空结果。两种场景均导致子agent任务失败。
aliases: IndexError list index out of range subagents.py
signals.review_reason: 两个issue共享 SubAgentMiddleware 的消息提取逻辑缺陷：场景1（#3046）在 LLM 超时/限流时崩溃 IndexError，场景2（#2857）在 Claude 返回空 end_turn 时静默返回空结果。子agent是 deepagents 核心多agent架构组成部分，任意一种失败均阻断父agent获取子agent结果，主流程阻断，有堆栈证据。

source_issues.title: `IndexError` in `SubAgentMiddleware` when LLM returns empty messages
source_issues.evidence: Crash at subagents.py line 411: result['messages'][-1] called without empty-list check. Triggers on any empty messages list from LLM (timeout, rate limit, zero-output model). State: closed (after fix), comments=6, is_recently_active=true.

source_issues.title: Fall back to the last non-empty AIMessage for subagents
source_issues.evidence: Anthropic Claude after tool result emits trailing empty end_turn AIMessage (output_tokens=0). Task-tool extractor only reads messages[-1].text, so parent receives '' instead of actual result. State: closed (after fix), comments=2, is_recently_active=true.

signals.topic: AgentCoreSandbox.download_files() 静默损坏二进制文件（双重base64解码 + ./路径解析失败）
signals.summary: download_files() 对二进制文件（PNG等）执行双重base64解码，导致返回损坏/截断数据（预期26KB变110字节），且 ./ 前缀路径总是返回 file_not_found，两个bug均在同一 _extract_files_from_stream 方法中，均为静默失败无报错。
signals.review_reason: 两个独立bug（双重base64解码 + ./路径不匹配）均属主流程阻断：用户无法从沙箱下载任何二进制文件（PNG图片、生成的图表等）并上传到外部系统。损坏完全静默（无异常），用户极难发现，导致错误数据在下游传播。关键功能不可用，有可复现样例。

source_issues.title: AgentCoreSandbox.download_files() silently corrupts binary files — double base64 decode + ./ path lookup failure in _extract_files_from_stream
source_issues.evidence: Bug 1: base64.b64decode() applied to raw bytes already decoded, corrupts PNG from ~26KB to ~110 bytes, silently with no error raised. Bug 2: ./-prefixed paths always return file_not_found even when file exists. Full reproduction code with matplotlib PNG save/load cycle included. State: open, is_recently_active=true.

signals.topic: QuickJS eval工具对 async IIFE 返回值不执行 await，导致返回未解析的 Promise handle 而非实际值
signals.summary: JavaScript 解释器支持顶层 await，但当 async IIFE 是最终表达式时，不会 await 返回的 Promise，导致 (async () => { return 123; })() 返回 [object] 而非 123。
aliases: async IIFE return value not awaited
signals.review_reason: eval 工具核心功能失效：当模型使用 async IIFE 模式（issue明确指出模型默认倾向此模式）时，解释器返回未解析的 Promise handle 而非实际值，导致 eval 结果错误。主流程阻断，有明确可复现代码样例。

source_issues.title: Bug: `eval` interpreter tool does not await async IIFE return values
source_issues.evidence: Two semantically equivalent code patterns produce different results: top-level await works (returns 123), async IIFE returns [object]/handle instead of 456. Issue explicitly states models lean towards IIFEs by default, so this affects a common code pattern. State: open, is_recently_active=true, comments=0.

signals.topic: PatchToolCallsMiddleware 无法处理 invalid_tool_calls 字段，触发 BadRequestError 导致 agent 调用完全失败
signals.summary: 当 LLM 输出因 token 溢出被截断导致 JSON 格式错误时，msg.invalid_tool_calls 被填充但没有对应 ToolMessage。PatchToolCallsMiddleware 只处理 msg.tool_calls，导致后续 API 调用因 'tool_calls must be followed by tool messages' 抛出 BadRequestError。
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：当 LLM 输出超限产生 invalid_tool_calls 时，agent.invoke() 抛出 BadRequestError 异常，整个 agent 调用失败。这是 deepseek 等模型 token 溢出场景下的高频触发路径，有明确 API 错误信息和修复方案。

source_issues.title: PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle msg.invalid_tool_calls without ToolMessage
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer: agent.invoke() with Deepseek model where output token overflow causes invalid_tool_calls. Error: BadRequestError('Error code: 400 - tool_calls must be followed by tool messages responding to each tool_call_id'). Workaround: manually patched loop to include invalid_tool_calls. State: closed (after fix), confirmed still present in latest commit. is_recently_active=true.

signals.topic: FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result 在重构 Command 对象时丢失 goto/graph 导航字段，导致多agent handoff 完全失效
signals.summary: 当工具返回 Command(goto=..., graph=Command.PARENT) 实现跨agent导航时，FilesystemMiddleware 在拦截大结果后重建 Command 只复制了 update 字段，丢失了 goto 和 graph，导致目标 agent 永远不会被执行。create_deep_agent 受影响，create_agent 正常。
signals.review_reason: 多agent工作流静默失败：父agent无法将控制权移交给子agent，目标agent永远不执行，且无任何报错，用户极难定位。create_deep_agent（deepagents核心API）受影响，create_agent 不受影响，对比鲜明。有完整端到端复现代码和 stream 日志证据。

source_issues.title: `FilesystemMiddleware._intercept_large_tool_result` drops `goto` and `graph` from Command objects
source_issues.evidence: End-to-end repro shows create_agent works (nodes: ['agent_a', 'agent_b']), create_deep_agent broken (nodes: ['agent_a'] only, agent_b never executes). Verified via stream(stream_mode='updates'). Bisected to FilesystemMiddleware. Unit test included. State: open, comments=4, is_recently_active=true.

signals.topic: stream_events(v3): reasoning content silently dropped from persisted AIMessage when message also contains tool_call, breaking conversation history
signals.summary: When using stream_events(version='v3') with reasoning-capable models (e.g. Gemini with thinking enabled), reasoning text streamed during a tool-calling turn is silently dropped from the final AIMessage in graph state. Live streaming via .reasoning works, but the persisted message — stored in checkpointers and returned on conversation read-back — loses all reasoning content. This breaks conversation history for all agent users relying on reasoning models with tool calls.
aliases: reasoning dropped from AIMessage with tool_calls
v3 stream drops reasoning on tool-calling turns
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues both confirm the same root cause in _finish() — reasoning blocks that don't receive an explicit content-block-finish before message-finish are silently dropped. User impact is significant: conversation history (checkpointers, read-back) loses all reasoning for every tool-calling turn on Gemini and similar reasoning models. This is not a cosmetic issue — persisted state is corrupted.

source_issues.title: stream_events(version="v3"): reasoning content dropped from AIMessage when message also contains a tool_call
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows reasoning streams live via .reasoning projection but is absent from final AIMessage.content/tool_calls after astream_events completes. Root cause: _finish() sweeps tool_call_chunks but has no equivalent sweep for _reasoning_per_block, so unterminated reasoning blocks never land in self._blocks. Affects all users with reasoning-capable models + tool calls.

source_issues.title: stream_events(version="v3"): reasoning content dropped from AIMessage when same message contains a tool_call
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproduction using ChatModelStream dispatch directly confirms silent data loss: content block contains only tool_call, reasoning text is gone and unrecoverable from saved message.

signals.topic: Chroma.update_document() raises ValueError when Document metadata is omitted, inconsistent with add_documents()
signals.summary: Calling ChromaVectorStore.update_document() with a Document that has no explicit metadata raises ValueError, while add_documents() accepts the same Document structure without complaint. This inconsistency breaks document update workflows and forces users to always pass metadata={} explicitly.
signals.review_reason: User-visible workflow blocker: document update fails where document add succeeds, for the exact same Document structure. Forces workaround of always passing metadata={}. Single issue but clear user impact on a core CRUD operation for Chroma vector stores.

source_issues.title: `Chroma.update_document()` fails when `Document` metadata is omitted
source_issues.evidence: User reports update_document() raises ValueError: 'Expected metadata to be a non-empty dict, got 0 metadata attributes in update.' add_documents() accepts Document(page_content='...') without metadata. The fix is normalizing document.metadata to {} before passing to Chroma API in update_documents(). Confirmed by 3 comment thread showing this is a real workflow blocker.

signals.topic: grep_search Python fallback silently skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() using OS default encoding
signals.summary: When ripgrep is unavailable, the Python fallback in grep_search uses file_path.read_text() with no explicit encoding. On Windows this defaults to cp1252 instead of UTF-8, causing valid UTF-8 files to raise UnicodeDecodeError and be silently skipped. Users on Windows get incomplete or empty grep results even when matching content exists.
signals.review_reason: Platform-specific but impactful: Windows users lose search results silently because UTF-8 files are skipped without warning. The silent 'continue' means users may not even know results are incomplete. Low-level tool issue, single repo impact.

source_issues.title: grep_search: Python fallback skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() encoding
source_issues.evidence: Windows user reports grep_search returns incomplete/empty results for UTF-8 markdown files. Root cause: read_text() with no encoding uses OS default (cp1252 on Windows), and files that fail to decode are silently skipped via 'except (UnicodeDecodeError, PermissionError): continue'. Cross-platform searches are unreliable on Windows whenever Python fallback path is taken.

signals.topic: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound requests, causing HTTP 400 on second turn of multi-turn / tool-using agent loops
signals.summary: ChatDeepSeek captures reasoning_content from API responses into AIMessage.additional_kwargs but fails to echo it back on outbound requests. DeepSeek reasoner models require the prior turn's reasoning_content to be sent on every multi-turn request. The second turn of any agent loop (create_react_agent, create_agent in LangGraph) raises openai.BadRequestError 400: 'The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API'.
aliases: DeepSeek reasoner model agent loop broken
reasoning_content not echoed to DeepSeek API
signals.review_reason: Clear user-facing API failure: any agent using DeepSeek reasoner models in a multi-turn loop (including create_react_agent and create_agent) crashes on the second turn with HTTP 400. This is a main-flow failure for DeepSeek reasoner users — the core agent use case is completely broken.

source_issues.title: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound requests, breaking multi-turn / tool-using flows with reasoner models
source_issues.evidence: User reports openai.BadRequestError 400 on second agent turn: 'The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.' Single-shot invoke() works; any agent loop that re-invokes the model after a tool result fails. 8 comments active. Contributor has a ready PR branch at fix/deepseek-echo-reasoning-content.

signals.topic: ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(..., method='json_schema').stream() drops response headers including x-request-id from response_metadata
signals.summary: When using with_structured_output with method='json_schema' in streaming mode, HTTP response headers (specifically x-request-id) are not propagated into response_metadata on streamed AIMessageChunk objects. This breaks request correlation for observability/tracing. The same works correctly for plain streaming and AzureChatOpenAI structured streaming.
aliases: x-request-id not in response_metadata json_schema method
signals.review_reason: Observability blocker: x-request-id is a standard header for correlating API requests with server logs. Its absence in this specific streaming path prevents users from debugging/production-tracing their structured output streaming calls. Clear regression from expected behavior.

source_issues.title: ChatOpenAI.with_structured_output(..., method="json_schema").stream() drops response headers / x-request-id in response_metadata
source_issues.evidence: User provides reproducible test showing x-request-id is captured for plain streaming but MISSING for streaming + with_structured_output(json_schema). 4 comments active. Affects observability — cannot correlate streamed requests with provider-side logs. Azure path works, regular path works; only the json_schema structured streaming path is broken.

signals.topic: Interrupt() inside while loop causes exponential extra resumes due to scratchpad.resume list accumulation
signals.summary: When interrupt() is called inside a while loop (a very common human-in-the-loop validation pattern), each resume causes the entire scratchpad.resume list to be replayed from the beginning, leading to exponentially growing redundant executions. The official docs pattern is affected. User confirmed the expected behavior vs actual behavior clearly.
aliases: scratchpad resume list accumulation in while loop
signals.review_reason: This is a core workflow runtime bug that directly breaks the most common human-in-the-loop pattern: validating user input in a while loop with interrupt(). The official docs explicitly show this pattern. The exponential re-execution causes significant cost waste (repeated LLM calls) and unpredictable behavior. Bug is confirmed with a self-contained reproducible example and clear expected vs actual output.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Interrupt() in a loop will cause extra resumes
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: user followed official docs pattern for human input validation. When calling graph.invoke(Command(resume="-1")) six times, the node executed 21 times total instead of 6 times (exponential growth). The scratchpad.resume ordered list does not account for multiple interrupt() calls within a single while loop iteration.

signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes without guard, causing error replay instead of retry (async path already fixed)
signals.summary: When using CachePolicy with the sync API, a task that fails or is interrupted has its error/INTERRUPT writes cached. On re-invocation with the same inputs, the cache replays those error writes as valid results, bypassing retry logic entirely. The async path already has a guard; the sync path is missing it.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime bug that silently corrupts retry behavior. When CachePolicy is used with the sync API and a node fails, the cache replays the error as a valid result on the next invocation, making the application appear to succeed while returning an error state. The async path was already fixed, indicating this is a known class of bug that was overlooked in the sync path. No workaround is available.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes at line 1203 persists task writes to cache unconditionally, missing the guard that AsyncPregelLoop.put_writes already has at line 1407. When CachePolicy is enabled and a node fails, the next invocation replays the error as a valid cached result instead of re-executing.

signals.topic: Runs.Stream.join drops all subgraph events when stream_mode query param is supplied (regression in joinStream endpoint)
signals.summary: The GET /threads/{thread_id}/runs/{run_id}/stream endpoint (joinStream) silently drops every subgraph stream event when the client supplies a stream_mode query param. The bug is a read-side vs write-side filter mismatch: write-side uses prefix matching (e.g., 'updates|subgraph:abc'), but read-side uses exact equality. This causes 100% of subgraph events to be lost on stream reconnection.
aliases: subgraph events lost on stream reconnect
signals.review_reason: This is a significant data loss regression that silently drops 100% of subgraph stream events when using the joinStream endpoint with stream_mode parameter. Users reconnecting to an ongoing run lose all subgraph event data. The reproducer includes a self-contained multi-file test that demonstrates the issue with a clear before/after comparison showing 12 events vs 0 events.

source_issues.title: langgraph-runtime-inmem: Runs.Stream.join drops subgraph events when stream_mode is supplied (joinStream regression)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: reproducer shows initial stream returns 12 subgraph events, but joinStream returns 0 subgraph events. AssertionError: 'BUG: joinStream returned ZERO subgraph events'. Root cause is in langgraph_runtime_inmem/ops.py: Runs.Stream.join uses exact equality for mode filtering while worker-side uses prefix matching. Affects langgraph-sdk, @langchain/langgraph-sdk (TypeScript), and langgraph-runtime-inmem.

signals.topic: allowed_msgpack_modules not honored — framework integration broken, causes AttributeError on resume
signals.summary: When integrating LangGraph via a framework (e.g., UiPath-Langchain) that sets allowed_msgpack_modules to enable strict mode for first-party types, user-defined models get degraded to plain dicts on resume, causing AttributeError at runtime. Users cannot properly register library types without enabling strict mode for user types.
aliases: JsonPlusSerializer strict mode degrades user models to dict
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks production framework integrations that use LangGraph as a backend. When a framework configures allowed_msgpack_modules to register its own types, all user types silently become plain dicts on resume, causing AttributeError at runtime. This is a key integration blocker for partners like UiPath. No workaround exists that preserves both framework type safety and user type integrity.

source_issues.title: Honor allowed_msgpack_modules in langgraph.json
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: self-contained reproducer shows that when a framework integrator sets allowed_msgpack_modules for its own types, user types (UserModel) are blocked from deserialization and degraded to dict, causing AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'label' at runtime on resume. Affects production framework integrations like UiPath.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after Overwrite in the same super-step
signals.summary: When multiple parallel nodes write to a BinaryOperatorAggregate channel in the same super-step and one of the writes is Overwrite followed by regular values, the subsequent regular values are silently dropped with no warning or error. This is dangerous silent data loss during state transitions.
aliases: BinaryOperatorAggregate silent data loss after Overwrite
Overwrite followed by regular values dropped
signals.review_reason: This is a dangerous silent data loss bug in a core channel type. When a user applies an Overwrite followed by regular values in the same super-step, the regular values are silently discarded with no error or warning. Since applying an operator after wiping state makes no logical sense, this should raise InvalidUpdateError instead of silently returning incorrect state. Data loss in state transitions is a severe user-impact issue.

source_issues.title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with self-contained reproducer: channel.update([5, Overwrite(10), 3]) results in value=10 instead of raising InvalidUpdateError. The '3' is completely silently lost. Expected behavior is InvalidUpdateError (cannot apply regular updates after overwriting in the same step).

signals.topic: LLM node fails with 'Invalid File' error when processing files or knowledge results
signals.summary: LLM nodes in workflows fail with 'Invalid File' or 'Invalid upload file' errors in multiple scenarios: when knowledge results retrieved from external Dify accounts via HTTP include the _source field, and intermittently during chatflow execution even when no file is uploaded at all. Both errors cause the LLM node to abort, blocking the main workflow.
signals.review_reason: 3 distinct issues all involving LLM node 'Invalid File' failures, affecting both Cloud and self-hosted deployments. #36231 is explicitly a regression, #36218 is intermittent but blocks chat flows, and #36214 is a deployment startup failure that prevents any workflow from running. Combined, these represent a widespread pattern of file validation errors at the LLM node level.

source_issues.title: LLM node failing with 'Invalid File' message
source_issues.evidence: On Dify Cloud, LLM node fails with 'invalid file' error when knowledge results from an external Dify account via HTTP include the _source field. Removing _source allows the workflow to succeed but breaks citation functionality. User describes it as a regression.

source_issues.title: Node llm failed with ABORT strategy: Invalid upload file
source_issues.evidence: Self-hosted Docker v1.14.1. Chat flow intermittently fails with LLM node error 'Invalid upload file' even when no file was uploaded. Log shows RuntimeError: Invalid upload file thrown at workflow execution entry.

source_issues.title: Failed to start api_websocket
source_issues.evidence: Docker compose up with default env fails. api_websocket container crashes with GeventWebSocketWorker class not found. All default Docker deployments are blocked from starting.

signals.topic: Flask application context error crashes LLM nodes in iteration/parallel workflow structures
signals.summary: When an LLM node with memory enabled is placed inside an iteration node running in parallel mode, the workflow crashes with 'RuntimeError: Working outside of application context' because the fetch_memory call attempts to access the Flask database session from a worker thread where no Flask context exists.
aliases: Flask context out of scope in LLM node
signals.review_reason: Single but highly specific issue with complete stack trace evidence. The Flask context error is a deterministic reproduction in a specific workflow composition (LLM+memory → iteration/parallel → LLM). While count=1, the crash is a main flow blocker for users building complex workflows with memory and parallel nodes, which is a core Dify use case.

source_issues.title: fetch memory of LLM node may cause out of flask context
source_issues.evidence: Self-hosted v1.4.1 (source). When LLM node with memory enabled is followed by an iteration node in parallel mode containing another LLM node, the workflow crashes with 'RuntimeError: Working outside of application context' at the fetch_memory call. Full stack trace provided showing the Flask context error propagating through node_factory.py.

signals.topic: Plugin upgrade silently breaks existing workflows by not updating version references
signals.summary: After upgrading a plugin to a newer version, existing workflows that reference the old plugin version via plugin_unique_identifier continue executing silently without errors, but the tool produces no output. Downstream nodes receive empty values, and users see incomplete results with no indication of failure.
signals.review_reason: Although count=1, the issue is explicitly marked as a recurring pattern (references 3 prior issues), and the silent failure behavior makes it especially dangerous. Users lose trust in their published workflows after plugin upgrades, with no error indication. This is a main flow failure that can go unnoticed in production.

source_issues.title: Plugin upgrade does not update existing workflow plugin_unique_identifier references, causing silent tool failure
source_issues.evidence: Self-hosted Docker v1.14.1. After upgrading a plugin from v2.1.0 to v3.6.9, existing workflows silently fail—the tool node produces no output, downstream answer nodes receive empty values, and the user sees 'DOCX file has been generated' text with no actual file attached. The issue references 3 prior related issues (#20756, #26991, #19032), indicating a recurring pattern.

signals.topic: Workflow run status remains 'running' after user-initiated termination
signals.summary: In both Dify Cloud and self-hosted v1.14.1, after a user terminates a running workflow, the status remains 'running' indefinitely instead of transitioning to a terminal state (stopped/failed). This blocks users from re-running workflows and causes confusion about actual execution state.
aliases: workflow stuck in running state after stop
signals.review_reason: Affects both Cloud and self-hosted deployments with video evidence. The stuck 'running' state blocks workflow re-execution and creates confusion about actual state. This is a main flow issue affecting the core workflow execution lifecycle.

source_issues.title: Workflow run remains running after being terminated in v1.14.1
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in both Dify Cloud v1.14.1 and self-hosted v1.14.1. Video evidence provided showing the workflow status remains 'running' after termination. User cannot re-run the workflow until manually resolving the stuck state.

signals.topic: Chatflow annotation reply UI gets stuck in loading/generating state after response output
signals.summary: When a Chatflow application with Annotation Reply enabled returns an annotation match, the chat interface remains in 'Generating' state (Stop Responding button visible, input blocked) after the text is fully displayed. Users must manually click 'Stop Responding' to proceed, blocking the next message.
aliases: annotation reply stuck in generating state
signals.review_reason: Clear user experience degradation affecting the core chat interaction loop. The annotation reply feature—a key Dify differentiator—is rendered unusable without manual intervention. Affects the main conversational flow.

source_issues.title: Chatflow App Annotation Reply stuck in loading state after outputting response (v1.14.1)
source_issues.evidence: Self-hosted Docker v1.14.1. After annotation reply is displayed, the chat UI stays in 'Generating' state with 'Stop Responding' button visible and input box disabled. Sending the next message shows warning 'Please wait for the response to the previous message to complete.' User is forced to manually stop.

signals.topic: Custom metadata silently dropped during memory.update() on all non-MongoDB vector stores
signals.summary: Memory.update() and AsyncMemory.update() silently drop all custom metadata fields (category, priority, source, bucket_id, etc.) that were originally stored during add(). Only a hard-coded whitelist of 5 session identifiers (user_id, agent_id, run_id, actor_id, role) is preserved — everything else is permanently lost.
signals.review_reason: Main flow data loss: users store structured metadata during add() but it silently disappears on update() with no warning. This is a regression from V3. Users lose data with no indication anything went wrong, making this a P0 blocking issue.

source_issues.title: _update_memory() still drops custom metadata on all non-MongoDB vector stores (follow-up from #4495 never completed, regressed in V3 pipeline)
source_issues.evidence: Memory.update() and AsyncMemory.update() silently drop all custom metadata fields (e.g. category, priority, source, bucket_id) that were originally stored during add(). Only a hard-coded whitelist of 5 session identifiers is preserved — everything else is permanently lost. Issue is a regression from V3 pipeline, with a prior attempt (#4495) that was never completed.

signals.topic: Graph memory poisoning allows attacker-controlled content to be retrieved as trusted agent context across user sessions
signals.summary: Untrusted interaction from one user is transformed into persistent graph-memory evidence, merged into an existing entity neighborhood, and later retrieved as trusted context for another user or agent session. In a healthcare assistant scenario, analogous failure could cause a user to take the wrong medication.
signals.review_reason: Critical integrity failure with concrete real-world harm scenario. Attacker content becomes persistent trusted agent context retrievable across user sessions. Researchers explicitly state analogous failure in healthcare could cause wrong medication — this meets the bar for P0 user impact even at count=1 because the harm scenario is specific and validated.

source_issues.title: Responsible Disclosure: High-Severity Vulnerability in Shared Graph-Based Agent Memory
source_issues.evidence: Responsible disclosure from security research team at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. Untrusted user input is transformed into persistent graph-memory evidence and retrieved as trusted context for another user. Concrete harm scenario: analogous failure in a healthcare assistant could cause a user to take the wrong medication. This is not theoretical — the researcher team has validated the attack chain.

signals.topic: memory.add() crashes with 400 Bad Request when conversation exceeds embedding token limit (8192 tokens)
signals.summary: When calling memory.add(), the library concatenates the full raw conversation into a single string and passes it directly to the embedding model. If the conversation exceeds 8192 tokens, the call fails with a 400 Bad Request before any memory is extracted or stored.
signals.review_reason: Main flow hard crash: memory.add() throws BadRequestError when conversation exceeds token limit. Users cannot add memories for any long conversation at all. The entire add operation is aborted with no partial storage or chunking fallback.

source_issues.title: Raw conversation text embedded for existing-memory retrieval causes token limit crash and poor recall on multi-topic conversations
source_issues.evidence: memory.add() concatenates full raw conversation into a single string and passes it to the embedding model without chunking. If the conversation exceeds 8192 tokens, the call fails with 400 Bad Request before any memory is extracted or stored. The entire operation is aborted with no fallback.

signals.topic: Missing authorization on POST /configure allows any API key holder to hijack global LLM/embedder configuration and exfiltrate all user data
signals.summary: The POST /configure endpoint modifies the global LLM provider configuration without authorization checks. Any holder of a distributed API key can redirect all LLM and embedder traffic to an attacker-controlled server, exfiltrating every user's prompts, memories, and embeddings.
aliases: global config writable by any API key holder
signals.review_reason: Critical security + availability failure: any API key holder can redirect ALL traffic to attacker-controlled endpoint, exfiltrating all user data. Global blast radius across entire deployment with persistence across restarts. Even at count=1, the severity (complete tenant isolation breach + data exfiltration) warrants P0.

source_issues.title: Missing Authorization on POST /configure Allows Any API Key Holder to Hijack Global LLM Configuration
source_issues.evidence: POST /configure endpoint has no authorization check. Any API key holder can redirect all LLM and embedder traffic to an attacker-controlled endpoint. Config is written to PostgreSQL and survives server restarts. This exfiltrates all user prompts, memories, and embeddings with global blast radius across the entire deployment.

npx mcp-add rejected by Claude Desktop

signals.topic: GroupChat round-robin skips the last agent when max_round is an even number

An off-by-one error causes the last agent to be systematically excluded whenever max_round is even, directly breaking multi-agent round-robin workflows — a primary use case of AutoGen. Two independent duplicate reports (same author, same hour) confirm the issue. While both issues were closed, the underlying algorithmic defect in the speaker selection logic represents a real functional failure for users relying on round-robin group conversations.

signals.topic: Codegen generated code for file input elements produces broken/invalid test scripts
signals.summary: Playwright codegen generates invalid code for <input type="file"> elements: it emits `click()` before `setInputFiles()` unnecessarily, leaving the OS file dialog open and causing the generated test to hang, and it omits the file path from `setInputFiles()` arguments so the generated script cannot be re-run.
aliases: codegen click+setInputFiles file input redundant click
codegen file input dialog left open
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues both describe codegen generating unusable test code for file inputs. #40855 omits file paths making re-runs impossible; #40854 emits a redundant `click()` that leaves the OS file dialog open, causing the generated test to hang. Together these block the core codegen-to-test-authoring workflow — a primary Playwright feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: The arguments for setInputFiles() generated by codegen do not include the file path.
source_issues.evidence: Codegen generates `setInputFiles()` with only filenames and no path. Generated script cannot be re-run in any environment where the original file path differs.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Codegen generates click() and setInputFiles() for operations on <input type="file"> elements, but only setInputFiles() is needed.
source_issues.evidence: Codegen emits both `click()` and `setInputFiles()`. The redundant `click()` opens a native file dialog that remains open after `setInputFiles()` executes, blocking the generated test. This is a main-flow test authoring failure.

signals.topic: Playwright emits Node.js DEP0205 deprecation warning on every test run under Node 26
signals.summary: On Node 26, `module.register()` triggers a [DEP0205] runtime deprecation warning per worker process, polluting CI logs with repeated warnings that will eventually become errors.
signals.review_reason: DEP0205 warnings pollute every CI run under Node 26 and will become hard errors in future Node versions, directly breaking test execution. This is an experience degradation + future-blocking issue. The related CI env-var docs gap (#40860) compounds the problem by providing misleading configuration examples.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: module.register() deprecation warning (DEP0205) on Node 26
source_issues.evidence: Node 26 emits [DEP0205] deprecation warning once per worker process on every test run. With default worker count, the same warning repeats N times in CI logs. This is not just noise — DEP warnings escalate to errors in future Node versions, meaning tests will break outright.

source_issues.title: [Docs]: Clarify `process.env.CI` truthiness in basic config
source_issues.evidence: Playwright's own docs recommend `process.env.CI ? 2 : 0` for retries, but Node env vars are always strings so `CI=false` is truthy. Users may misconfigure CI settings based on Playwright's own examples, causing incorrect retry/worker behavior.

signals.topic: @playwright/mcp reports wrong missing executable in error message
signals.summary: When ffmpeg is missing (required for video recording), the MCP tool reports 'Browser chrome is not installed' instead of naming ffmpeg as the missing dependency, wasting developer time with a misleading error.
aliases: MCP ffmpeg missing error message wrong
signals.review_reason: Users are actively misled by a false error message. The MCP tool declares chrome missing when chrome IS installed, hiding the actual root cause (missing ffmpeg). This causes significant debugging time loss and blocks the video recording workflow. Root cause is precisely identified in the codebase.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @playwright/mcp reports "Browser "chrome" is not installed" when ffmpeg is actually the missing executable
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: `browserFactory.ts` substring-matches 'Executable doesn't exist' on any launch error and unconditionally rethrows via `throwBrowserIsNotInstalledError` naming the browser channel. When `recordVideo` is set and ffmpeg is missing, Playwright's registry produces the 'Executable doesn't exist' message for ffmpeg, but the error is rethrown as 'Browser chrome is not installed'. Verified with a Docker repro.

signals.topic: Compound ANSI SGR color codes are silently dropped in HTML reporter and trace viewer
signals.summary: Terminal color codes from modern libraries (chalk, picocolors, vitest, jest, eslint) are silently stripped from error output in Playwright's HTML reporter and trace viewer, making error messages unreadable.
aliases: ANSI color codes dropped in HTML reporter
compound SGR codes not rendered in trace viewer
signals.review_reason: Error messages are a critical debugging surface. When compound ANSI codes (the default output of chalk, picocolors, vitest, jest, eslint) are silently dropped, the actual error text is present but unstyled — users lose the visual hierarchy that makes error messages parseable. This directly impairs the primary debugging workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Compound ANSI SGR codes lose styling in HTML reporter and trace viewer
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: `ansi2html.ts` does `+codeStr` on compound codes like '1;31', producing NaN, causing no switch case to match and silently dropping the entire sequence. Affects vitest snapshot diffs, jest, prettier, eslint output — the most common sources of test error messages. The DOM receives no styling at all.

signals.topic: AggregateError.errors[] sub-errors are silently dropped from test reporter output
signals.summary: When a test throws an AggregateError (e.g., teardown failures from multiple cleanup operations), only the top-level message appears in the reporter; the individual errors in .errors[] are silently dropped.
signals.review_reason: AggregateError is the standard pattern for reporting multiple concurrent failures (teardown, fixture cleanup, Promise.allSettled). When sub-errors are dropped, developers lose the only evidence of what actually failed. This directly blocks debugging of multi-failure scenarios.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `AggregateError.errors[]` sub-errors are invisible in reporter output — only the top-level message is serialized
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: `filterStackTrace` in `util.ts` recurses through `e.cause` but never walks `e.errors[]`. AggregateError is idiomatic for surfacing multiple failures (e.g., `Promise.allSettled`, fixture teardown). When teardown fails for multiple fixtures, the developer sees only 'teardown failed' with no details about which fixtures or why.

signals.topic: .NET PgVector NuGet package version 1.75.0 missing from NuGet Gallery, blocking use of VectorSearchOptions

signals.topic: Handlebars template execution_settings (max_tokens, temperature) ignored when PromptExecutionSettings with ServiceId is passed

The LLM falls back to its own defaults, producing longer/more uncontrolled output than intended.
aliases: PromptExecutionSettings overrides template settings entirely instead of merging
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug with clear user-impact evidence: template-defined execution settings are silently discarded when a PromptExecutionSettings object is provided at function creation time, causing unpredictable LLM output. The workaround forces users to choose between dynamic ServiceId selection and template-defined defaults — a broken either/or that disrupts agent configuration workflows. Reproducible with minimal steps, root cause identified in code.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Handlebars Template execution_settings Ignored When Passing PromptExecutionSettings with ServiceId
source_issues.evidence: Bug is explicitly reproducible: when PromptExecutionSettings with only ServiceId is passed to CreateFunctionFromPrompt, the template's max_tokens=10 and temperature=1.0 are ignored. Output is 'significantly longer than 10 tokens' confirming max_tokens was ignored. Root cause traced to KernelFunctionFromPrompt.cs code that replaces entire execution_settings dict instead of merging.

signals.topic: Kernel.Invoke does not execute plugin functions referenced in Handlebars YAML prompt templates

This blocks a primary use case of combining prompt templates with registered plugins, which is fundamental to Semantic Kernel's design. Count=1 but impact is high — it breaks the intended template-function integration pattern.

signals.topic: Realtime known tool failures do not send model-visible output causing model to hang

signals.review_reason: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output, causing the model to wait indefinitely (~30 seconds) until server-side timeout. Main flow is blocked - session appears to hang. Clear main flow blocking with reproduction steps provided.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output

signals.review_reason: Voice text splitter silently drops short text chunks (<20 chars) even when custom splitter explicitly marks text as ready. User's valid responses like 'ok' are lost. Experience degradation through data loss in voice interactions.

signals.topic: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped

signals.review_reason: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped, falling back to generic 'Tool execution was not approved' message instead of the callback's specific reason. Users don't see why their action was rejected - moderate UX degradation.

source_issues.title: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped

signals.topic: OpenClaw-Claude ACP spawn path fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED, blocking two-agent orchestration
signals.summary: OpenClaw `/acp spawn claude` fails with `ACP_TURN_FAILED / UNAVAILABLE / Internal error` while the same Claude agent works fine via direct `acpx claude`. This directly blocks the automatic Codex + Claude two-agent ACP flow that OpenClaw is designed to enable.
signals.review_reason: 用户主流程阻断：OpenClaw spawn claude 完全不可用，底层 Claude agent 本身正常，说明是 OpenClaw ACP 层的集成问题而非环境问题，直接导致用户无法通过 OpenClaw 启动 Claude 辅助 agent，无法实现自动化的 Codex+Claude 双 agent 工作流。count=1 降为 P1。

source_issues.title: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude fails with ACP_TURN_FAILED while direct acpx claude succeeds
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw /acp spawn claude returns ACP_TURN_FAILED / UNAVAILABLE / Internal error; direct acpx claude succeeds from the same host; Gateway probe, Codex standard ACP, Claude CLI no-write smoke all pass; only the OpenClaw spawn path fails, blocking automatic two-agent ACP flow.

signals.topic: Claude ACP config option key mismatch causes turn failures for runtime controls like timeout and thinking
signals.summary: When OpenClaw applies generic runtime controls (timeoutSeconds, thinking) as ACP session/set_config_option calls, Claude ACP rejects them due to key mismatches, resulting in ACP_TURN_FAILED / Internal error. Clean prompts and model overrides work, but any runtime control breaks.
aliases: config option key mismatch Claude ACP
signals.review_reason: 用户主流程阻断（部分场景）：当用户通过 OpenClaw 使用带超时或 thinking 配置的 Claude ACP 时，turn 完全失败并抛出 Internal error。这意味着需要任何运行时控制（超时、推理 effort）的用户场景全部被阻断，workaround 只能是使用 clean/model-only 的极简路径，严重限制了 Claude ACP 的实用价值。count=1 降为 P1。

source_issues.title: Claude ACP config option handling: generic runtime controls fail while clean/model-only path works
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw maps timeoutSeconds to ACP key 'timeout' and thinking to 'thinking', neither of which Claude ACP advertises (Claude ACP uses 'effort' for reasoning). timeoutSeconds:180, thinking:medium/high all fail with AcpRuntimeError:Internal error / ACP_TURN_FAILED. Clean prompt and model override succeed. Fix likely requires acpx/OpenClaw to filter against adapter-advertised configOptionKeys before forwarding.

signals.topic: Session history/read APIs do not reflect live streamed assistant and tool events during active turns
signals.summary: acpx sessions history and sessions read only show the user prompt entry during an in-flight turn. Assistant messages, tool calls, and tool outputs that are already written to the Codex rollout JSONL on disk are not reflected in session history until the turn finishes. This breaks programmatic polling for live progress without attaching to stdout.
aliases: session history incomplete during active turn
live turn progress not visible in sessions history
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：对于程序化编排（agent-to-agent、多 session 并行监控）场景，sessions history 是 polling 进展的自然接口，但当前仅显示 user prompt，assistant/tool 事件全部缺失。虽然 agent 本身在正常运行（rollout log 有数据），但用户被迫直接解析 rollout JSONL，失去了 acpx session 抽象的价值。属于关键功能体验缺陷而非完全阻断，P2。

source_issues.title: ACP session history only records prompts while Codex is running
source_issues.evidence: During an active Codex turn, sessions history shows only the user prompt. The rollout JSONL on disk contains assistant messages, tool calls, tool outputs, and file edits. The sessions history/read APIs miss all streamed assistant/tool events until turn completion. agentSessionId also remains '-' in-flight. This breaks the natural polling API for detached/orchestrated workflows (--no-wait --file -).

signals.topic: External data ingestion without sanitization combined with authenticated privileged actions creates consistent prompt injection attack surface across 11 skills
signals.summary: 11 separate skills ingest external attacker-controlled data without sanitization while granting authenticated privileged mutations, enabling prompt injection chains across diverse domains.
signals.review_reason: 11 separate skills share the same structural pattern: external attacker-controlled data (analytics fields, code problem statements, GitHub issue content, community solutions, Workspace content, telemetry, HTML, SMS/notifications, tweets, customer records, unauthenticated network endpoints) is ingested into the agent context without sanitization, and each skill simultaneously grants authenticated privileged actions (site mutations, Bash execution, gh actions, Gmail/Drive/Sheets/Docs, Sentry resolve, Python execution, SMS/call, blockchain transactions, Shopify product deletion, shell access). Any external party who controls the ingested data can steer the agent to perform privileged actions under the user's authorization. This is a high-frequency (count=11), high-severity structural vulnerability pattern in the ClawHub ecosystem. P1 rather than P0 because it affects installed skills rather than blocking ClawHub's own core browsing/install main flow.

source_issues.title: Security: yogesharc/supalytics returns raw visitor-controlled analytics fields (UTM, referrer, page) into agent context, exposing authenticated supalytics sites mutations
source_issues.evidence: Visitor-controllable UTM parameters, referrer, and page data from Supalytics analytics API flows unsanitized into agent context. The same skill grants authenticated site-management mutations (add/update/remove site). Any external site visitor can poison analytics dimensions and steer the agent to mutate tracked sites.

source_issues.title: Security: wd1993/algorithm-solver feeds attacker-suppliable problem statements into code-generation, then executes the generated Python via Bash
source_issues.evidence: User-supplied problem text flows directly into code generation, and the resulting code is executed via Bash with the agent's local permissions. An attacker can embed prompt injection in a problem description to cause arbitrary code execution.

source_issues.title: Security: tsiontesfayechromaway/tester pipes raw GitHub issue and PR review content into authenticated gh-driven sub-agent workflow, exposing repository mutations
source_issues.evidence: Raw GitHub issue and PR review content is ingested and interpolated into sub-agent task strings. The same skill grants authenticated gh CLI authority including gh pr comment. Any user who can open an issue or comment on a PR can inject instructions that steer authenticated GitHub actions.

source_issues.title: Security: tomasz-tomczyk/reposit pulls community-submitted solutions into the coding agent's context on proactive search, exposing coding-agent tool authority
source_issues.evidence: The skill instructs the agent to proactively search community-submitted solutions on errors and applies those solutions with the coding agent's full tool authority. An attacker who submits a malicious 'solution' targeting a common error can steer the agent to read secrets, run commands, or exfiltrate files.

source_issues.title: Security: steipete/gog ingests raw Google Workspace content (Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Sheets/Docs) into agent context, exposing authenticated cross-product mutations
source_issues.evidence: Raw Gmail content, Calendar invites, Drive filenames, Sheets cell values, and Docs text are ingested without sanitization. The same skill grants authenticated Gmail send, Sheets update/append/clear, and Docs export under broad OAuth scope. Any third party who can deliver content to a Workspace surface the user reads can plant prompt injection text.

source_issues.title: Security: sergical/sentry-observability prints raw Sentry issue/event/log telemetry into agent context, exposing authenticated Sentry CLI actions during incident investigation
source_issues.evidence: Sentry issue titles, event context, and log messages containing remote-attacker-controllable fields (request paths, headers, usernames) are ingested without sanitization. The same agent has Sentry CLI authority for resolve and plan operations. Anyone who can make the monitored service emit a telemetry record can inject instructions.

source_issues.title: Security: seanwyngaard/web-scraper-as-a-service feeds attacker-controlled target-page HTML into code-generation, then executes the generated python scraper locally
source_issues.evidence: Target page HTML is used directly as code-generation input, and the resulting scraper is immediately executed locally with the agent's permissions. Any site the user asks to scrape can plant prompt injection in HTML to influence the generated code.

source_issues.title: Security: satyajiit/aster forwards raw Android SMS and notification text into the AI agent webhook message field, exposing authenticated phone-control tools
source_issues.evidence: Android SMS and notification text fields are packed into the agent webhook message without sanitization. The same agent holds authenticated tools for send_sms, make_call, input_text, and read_sms. Anyone who can SMS or push a notification to the paired phone can inject instructions.

source_issues.title: Security: samj12/betbud-prediction-market-creation feeds raw trending crypto tweets into Claude prompt that drives Base Sepolia openNewMarket and betbud.live registration
source_issues.evidence: Trending crypto tweets are ingested without sanitization and used to construct the market-proposal prompt. The resulting JSON signs a Base Sepolia transaction (openNewMarket) and registers on betbud.live. Any X user who can get a tweet to match the query parameters can steer on-chain market creation.

source_issues.title: Security: robsannaa/shopify-admin ingests raw Shopify order and customer JSON into agent context, exposing authenticated Shopify Admin actions including delete-product
source_issues.evidence: Customer names, addresses, order notes, and UTM/referral fields from Shopify Admin API are returned without sanitization. The same skill exposes authenticated delete-product. Any user who places an order or creates a customer record can plant prompt injection text in those fields to steer product deletion.

source_issues.title: Security: rendis/opcode exposes unauthenticated MCP/SSE endpoint on :4100 with auto-registered agents and built-in shell.exec, enabling remote code execution
source_issues.evidence: Opcode exposes shell.exec on a network-reachable TCP port with auto-registration and permissive defaults. Any caller who can reach :4100 can register an agent_id and execute arbitrary shell commands. The unauthenticated network surface combined with privileged shell access creates a direct RCE path.

signals.topic: API pagination non-functional on /api/v1/skills, preventing programmatic skill discovery beyond first page
signals.summary: API pagination returns identical first-page results regardless of cursor value across all sort modes, blocking all API-based automation and third-party integrations from discovering more than 10 skills.
signals.review_reason: The /api/v1/skills endpoint is ClawHub's primary API for programmatic skill discovery. Returning identical first-page results regardless of cursor means no consumer can access skills beyond the first 10 — the entire catalog beyond page 1 is unreachable via the API. This is a complete main-flow failure for all API-based tooling, integrations, and automation built on ClawHub. P0 despite count=1 because it blocks ClawHub's own core browsing/main-flow API.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Pagination not working on /api/v1/skills
source_issues.evidence: Every request to /api/v1/skills returns identical first-page results regardless of cursor. Passing the server's own advertised nextCursor back yields byte-identical response. Verified with curl + diff showing BYTE-IDENTICAL responses across all sort modes.

signals.topic: Skill install events never reported to registry, installsAllTime and installsCurrent permanently zero for all skills
signals.summary: clawhub install never sends install events to the registry, leaving popularity metrics broken for every skill on the marketplace.
signals.review_reason: Install tracking is absent from the entire install flow — clawhub install never reports events to the registry, so installsAllTime and installsCurrent remain permanently 0 for every skill. This prevents authors from seeing adoption metrics and users from making informed installation decisions based on popularity, representing significant experience degradation across the entire marketplace.

source_issues.title: installsAllTime / installsCurrent always 0 — install event not reported to registry
source_issues.evidence: clawhub install downloads skill files and writes local metadata but never POSTs install events to the registry. Backend data model (Convex schema) already has installsAllTime/installsCurrent fields ready; the CLI-to-registry reporting link is entirely absent.

signals.topic: Legitimate defensive security plugin incorrectly blocked as Malicious due to stale VirusTotal cache with no automated refresh
signals.summary: slowmist/slowmist-agent-security remains flagged Malicious after VirusTotal cleared the false positive; ClawHub never refreshed its cached verdict.
signals.review_reason: A legitimate defensive security plugin is incorrectly blocked on ClawHub because the VirusTotal cache was never refreshed after the false positive was cleared on VirusTotal's side. This makes a real security tool effectively undiscoverable and uninstalable, directly harming users who need it. The overall Malicious label persists despite ClawScan and static analysis both passing.

source_issues.title: [False Positive] slowmist-agent-security still marked Malicious after VirusTotal false positive was cleared
source_issues.evidence: slowmist/slowmist-agent-security is a defensive security review framework but is blocked as 'Malicious' due to a stale VirusTotal cache. The false positive was cleared on VirusTotal's end; ClawHub's cached verdict was never refreshed. ClawScan and static analysis both pass.

signals.topic: Skill indexing sync failure causes legitimate skill to show 'Skill not found' despite being publicly indexed and returning HTTP 200
signals.summary: jjr-iot-skill index returns HTTP 200 but its page shows 'Skill not found' with no search results, a persistent problem re-opened after #2047.
signals.review_reason: A legitimately published skill is completely inaccessible — the page shows 'Skill not found' despite being in the index and returning HTTP 200. This blocks discovery and installation, making the skill effectively unavailable to users. The re-open status confirms this is a persistent, recurring problem rather than a one-off glitch.

source_issues.title: [RE-OPEN REQUEST] Indexing sync failure for jjr-iot-skill (Previous #2047)
source_issues.evidence: Skill is indexed publicly and the index returns HTTP 200, yet the page displays 'Skill not found' and searching for the skill or its publisher janeXlab yields no results. This is a re-opened issue following #2047, indicating a persistent indexing or caching problem spanning multiple weeks.

signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: PR creation is a core developer workflow that fails without workaround, preventing code changes from being submitted through the automated system.

source_issues.title: [aw] Repo Assist failed
source_issues.evidence: Code push safe output failed with create_pull_request failing to apply bundle, cancelling all subsequent safe outputs and blocking the PR creation workflow entirely.

signals.topic: Long-running node capabilities block gateway health and pair messages (no back-pressure)
signals.summary: Sequential message processing blocks health pings during long-running operations like screen.record or system.run, causing gateway to incorrectly detect node death and tear down sessions; pair events arriving during long stt.transcribe are queued indefinitely.
aliases: Head-of-line blocking in WS receive loop
Health ping blocked by slow capability
Gateway thinks node is dead during captures
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation: users experience apparent disconnections during long captures, auto-pair flows stall, and gateway may prematurely tear down sessions; stop button cannot even be pressed to cancel because pair events are blocked.

source_issues.title: WindowsNodeClient single-threaded receive loop has no back-pressure (head-of-line blocking)
source_issues.evidence: Sequential message processing blocks health pings during long-running operations like screen.record or system.run, causing gateway to incorrectly detect node death and tear down sessions; pair events arriving during long stt.transcribe are queued indefinitely.

signals.topic: RTL language support and High Contrast accessibility entirely absent
signals.summary: FlowDirection and HighContrast have 0 occurrences in the entire codebase; app is unusable for RTL locale users (ar-SA, he-IL, fa-IR) and users with high-contrast vision needs who rely on Windows High Contrast theme.
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailability: RTL locale users cannot use the app meaningfully as text flows LTR over RTL strings with misaligned buttons and reversed chevrons; users with high-contrast vision needs cannot use the app at all as custom Mica backdrops ignore system theme.

source_issues.title: RTL and HighContrast support entirely absent (FlowDirection and HighContrast appear 0 times)
source_issues.evidence: FlowDirection and HighContrast have 0 occurrences in the entire codebase; app is unusable for RTL locale users (ar-SA, he-IL, fa-IR) and users with high-contrast vision needs who rely on Windows High Contrast theme.

signals.topic: Operator tray UI inaccessible to screen reader users
signals.summary: Only 3 instances of actual screen-reader label (AutomationProperties.Name) versus 46 test hooks (AutomationId); screen reader users get generic Button/TextBlock/Image instead of meaningful labels across the entire operator UI surface.
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation: screen reader users cannot navigate the operator UI which is the primary surface for gateway status, sessions, settings, deep-link approvals, and command-center diagnostics; the custom lobster emoji title bar is read as 'lobster' by Narrator with no context.

source_issues.title: Operator tray UI has 46 AutomationId test hooks but only 3 AutomationProperties.Name
source_issues.evidence: Only 3 instances of actual screen-reader label (AutomationProperties.Name) versus 46 test hooks (AutomationId); screen reader users get generic Button/TextBlock/Image instead of meaningful labels across the entire operator UI surface.

signals.topic: Stop/cancel button does not work on long-running capabilities via gateway transport
signals.summary: Capabilities that support cancellation (screen.record for 300s, camera.clip for 60s, system.run for up to 10min) receive CancellationToken.None when invoked via gateway transport, making the stop button completely non-functional for gateway-initiated operations.
aliases: Cancel button non-functional for long operations
Stop button does nothing during captures
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation: users cannot cancel screen recording, camera capture, or shell execution once started via the gateway transport, wasting up to 10 minutes of waiting and generating unwanted output files.

source_issues.title: CancellationToken contract exists on INodeCapability but WindowsNodeClient never passes one
source_issues.evidence: Capabilities that support cancellation (screen.record for 300s, camera.clip for 60s, system.run for up to 10min) receive CancellationToken.None when invoked via gateway transport, making the stop button completely non-functional for gateway-initiated operations.

signals.topic: Telegram group interactive session responses silently fail — responses never delivered
signals.summary: Telegram group bot receives messages and agent processes them but responses are silently dropped. Bot shows typing indicator but no sendMessage is called. Session log shows deliveryContext.to in string format instead of numeric.
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking for Telegram group users: messages are received and processed by the agent but responses are never delivered to the group. Bot shows typing but the user receives nothing. This is a clear conversation-flow failure where the agent works but output never reaches the user.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Telegram group interactive responses silently fail — session response delivery not fixed in v2026.5.16-beta.2
source_issues.evidence: Telegram group bot receives messages but responses are silently dropped. Agent generates responses but no sendMessage is called. Bot shows 'typing' indicator but nothing arrives. Session log shows deliveryContext.to in string format instead of numeric.

signals.topic: Event-loop starvation from memorySearch blocking all agents when embedding endpoint is slow
signals.summary: memorySearch performs vector query and remote embedding with no timeout, causing event-loop stalls that block ALL agents on the host. Telegram polling delays of 30–120s during stall windows.
signals.review_reason: Critical infrastructure failure that cascades to all users: event-loop starvation blocks ALL agents on the host (reported with 8 agents), not just one session. Telegram polling delays of 30-120s affect every user of the gateway. This is a systemic availability degradation.

source_issues.title: memorySearch + embedding-provider missing AbortController/circuit-breaker pattern from #65517 — event-loop starvation persists post-#74054
source_issues.evidence: 89 distinct event loop stalled >1s events in journalctl, max single-stall 50.7s. memorySearch performs vector query -> remote embedding -> vector index lookup with no timeout, can indefinitely block event loop. Telegram message delivery delays of 30-120s during stall windows.

signals.topic: Async exec completion triggers 5–42x duplicate Telegram messages per request
signals.summary: Every async exec completion in parallel sessions generates duplicate message deliveries. Duplication count grows with each test (2x, 5x, 17x, 42x). Each task_delivery_state entry spawns a separate session delivering the same message.
signals.review_reason: Blocks workflow: every exec-based skill response is duplicated 5–42 times, causing Telegram spam and extra API cost per duplicate LLM turn. This is significant UX degradation AND clear cost impact on every async exec call.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Multiple parallel sessions deliver duplicate messages for every async exec completion
source_issues.evidence: Every async exec completion triggers multiple parallel agent sessions, each delivering the same message to Telegram. The duplication count grows with each test (2x, 5x, 17x, 42x observed in one session). Each task_delivery_state entry generates a separate session.

signals.topic: Session model override to non-thinking Ollama model causes silent conversation death
signals.summary: Switching session to a non-thinking Ollama model causes OpenClaw to send thinking enabled, Ollama rejects with 400, runtime falls back to next=none, emits no content and no error. User sees complete silence.
signals.review_reason: Main-flow blocking: a single ordinary user action (switching session model) can make the conversation appear completely dead with no visible diagnostic. User has no way to understand what happened — indistinguishable from other silent defects. Clear UX degradation.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: switching session modelOverride to non-thinking Ollama model can silently kill the conversation (thinking 400, failover next=none)
source_issues.evidence: After switching session to ollama/qwen2.5:14b, OpenClaw sends thinking enabled but Ollama rejects with 400 'does not support thinking'. Runtime logs failover with next=none, emits no assistant content, sends no user-visible error. User sees complete silence.

signals.topic: Heartbeat polls interrupt model streaming responses causing wrong content delivery
signals.summary: Heartbeat poll arrives between user message and model response during streaming, gets inserted between them, delaying or reordering the model's reply. Users see heartbeat reply instead of expected model response.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation during core chat interaction: users receive incorrect content (heartbeat response) instead of their actual model response during active streaming. This disrupts the primary use case of reading model output.

source_issues.title: Heartbeat polls still interrupt model responses during streaming (not just tool calls)
source_issues.evidence: Heartbeat poll arrives between user message and model response, gets inserted between them, and the model's actual reply is delayed or appears out of order. Users see heartbeat reply instead of expected model response during streaming text output.

signals.topic: WhatsApp Dispatch integration silently fails — messages marked read but no action triggered
signals.summary: WhatsApp Dispatch shows 'Connected' status but fails to process incoming messages. Messages sent to self-chat are marked as read (blue ticks) but the interpreter core never receives the message data, leaving the application idle and non-functional for WhatsApp-triggered workflows.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine workflow-level failure. The WhatsApp Dispatch integration silently fails — it correctly marks messages as read via the headless browser but never passes the message data to the LLM for execution, making the entire WhatsApp-triggered workflow non-functional. The user has provided a clear reproduction path and screenshot evidence confirming the 'Connected' status with zero interpreter response.

source_issues.title: WhatsApp Dispatch connected but not processing or sending messages windows
source_issues.evidence: Messages are marked as read (double blue ticks) on the mobile device but no action is triggered in the desktop application's main console. The application stays idle on the 'What would you like to work on?' screen. The bridge between the WhatsApp Web instance and the interpreter core is broken — the headless browser reads messages but data is not passed to the LLM for execution.

signals.topic: tree_sitter QueryError in repomap.py causes uncaught crash at startup on Python 3.12

signals.review_reason: count=2, 同一代码路径（repomap.py:302）在两个不同平台（Linux/macOS）均触发未捕获异常，Python 3.12 兼容性问题是根因，阻断用户主流程（coder.run()），属于主流程崩溃。

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302

aliases: silent config load failure in benchmark
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但 review_reason 提供明确强证据：用户花费数小时调试、GPU 运行时浪费、benchmark 静默挂起数小时。LONG_TIMEOUT=24h 使失败模式极其隐蔽，属于关键功能不可用 + 明显成本损失。虽然单仓单 issue，满足 keep 条件。

source_issues.title: benchmark.py uses `--read-model-settings` but main cli + docs say `--model-settings-file`
source_issues.evidence: 用户花费数小时调试 polyglot bench 配置，根因是 benchmark.py 读取错误 flag 导致 YAML 配置静默失效。Qwen AWQ 模型因缺少 min_p/top_p 参数在长解码循环中挂起，外在表现是 bench 静默挂起数小时而非报错，benchmark.py 中 LONG_TIMEOUT=24h 导致问题难以感知。明确计费损失（GPU 运行时浪费）+ 关键功能不可用（benchmark 无法正常完成）。

signals.topic: 长 system-prompt 触发 OSError 导致未捕获崩溃

pathlib OSError crash with long arguments

source_issues.evidence: Uncaught OSError [Errno 63] File name too long at pathlib.py:1222 — main.py:692 将 --system-prompt 值传入 Path().is_dir() 导致崩溃。Python 3.9.6, macOS 25.4.1。应用启动即崩溃，无任何用户可处理路径。

signals.review_reason: count=1 但属主流程阻断性崩溃（startup 阶段即触发），aiohttp 依赖版本冲突导致 AttributeError，Windows 用户无法启动程序。属于 startup_crash + 关键功能不可用。

signals.topic: rag-poisoning redteam plugin evaluation fails with 'Unknown grader' error, blocking red team scans
signals.summary: When using the rag-poisoning redteam plugin, test case generation succeeds but evaluation fails for all generated test cases with 'Invariant failed: Unknown grader: promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning'. The plugin is registered as a remote plugin but no corresponding grader is registered in src/redteam/graders.ts, causing 100% error rate on all rag-poisoning test evaluations.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker for the rag-poisoning redteam plugin. Test case generation succeeds but all evaluations fail with an uncaught grader registration mismatch, resulting in 100% error rate. Users cannot complete red team scans with rag-poisoning without manual workaround. Clear user-impact evidence: the error is reproducible, blocks the core red team scan flow, and no automatic resolution is available.

source_issues.title: Bug: `rag-poisoning` tests fail during evaluation with `Unknown grader`
source_issues.evidence: 100% error rate (2/2 test cases) during red team evaluation with 'Invariant failed: Unknown grader: promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning'. Both echo target and AnythingLLM HTTP target repros fail identically. Workaround requires manually replacing generated assertions with llm-rubric.

signals.topic: Homebrew installation on darwin-arm64 fails with '@esbuild/darwin-arm64' not found, blocking promptfoo startup
signals.summary: Users who install promptfoo via Homebrew on Apple Silicon (darwin-arm64) encounter an esbuild binary resolution error at startup, preventing promptfoo from running any commands including code-scans.
aliases: esbuild darwin-arm64 binary not found homebrew
esbuild optional dep missing on apple silicon
signals.review_reason: This is a complete startup blocker for Apple Silicon Mac users installing via Homebrew. Promptfoo crashes before any command can execute, making the entire tool unusable for this install path. The esbuild optional dependency resolution fails during Homebrew's node_modules bundling. User impact is immediate and total: no promptfoo command works after Homebrew install on darwin-arm64.

source_issues.title: The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found
source_issues.evidence: Running 'brew install promptfoo' followed by 'promptfoo code-scans run' crashes immediately with 'The package "@esbuild/darwin-arm64" could not be found, and is needed by esbuild'. The error is triggered at promptfoo startup on macOS Apple Silicon via Homebrew installation.

signals.topic: undici 7 upgrade causes fetch to return uncompressed (raw Brotli/gzip) bytes, breaking JSON parsing on all compressed API responses
signals.summary: After upgrading to undici 7 (shipped in 0.121.x), promptfoo's pooled fetchWithProxy returns raw compressed bytes instead of decoded JSON when the remote endpoint returns Content-Encoding: gzip or br. This causes 'Unexpected token' JSON parse errors on essentially every compressed API response, particularly affecting OpenAI responses API and web-search-enabled evaluations.
aliases: undici 7 custom Agent missing decompress interceptor
signals.review_reason: This is a significant regression introduced by the undici 7 upgrade. All compressed API responses fail to parse, breaking the core evaluation workflow for any provider hitting OpenAI's CDN or other servers that compress responses. The symptom is a JSON parse error with binary garbage in the error message, affecting essentially every web-search eval call. The issue has a known per-provider workaround but no default fix shipped yet, making it a clear user pain point with visible failure evidence.

source_issues.title: fetch() with custom undici Agent does not decompress Content-Encoding responses (Brotli/gzip → garbage)
source_issues.evidence: All evaluations hitting OpenAI CDN (which uses Brotli compression on responses >~200 B) fail with 'Error parsing response... Received text: <binary>'. The binary is raw Brotli stream (first byte 0x1B/0x0B/0x0F). Particularly severe on web-search-enabled evals where all responses are large and always compressed. Triggered by undici v7 upgrade (PR #7137). A per-provider workaround (Accept-Encoding: identity) is known but not a default fix.

signals.topic: SimpleChatEngine astream_chat crashes with ValueError when ChatMessage has multiple blocks
signals.summary: When using SimpleChatEngine with astream_chat and calling get_full_response(), the application crashes with ValueError because awrite_response_to_history attempts to assign a multi-block ChatMessage to .content, which only supports single text blocks.
signals.review_reason: Stream consumption failure causes app crash in SimpleChatEngine — a core workflow is broken. Reproducible with clear stack trace and error message. Not P0 because single issue, single repo.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks in SimpleChatEngine
source_issues.evidence: Crashes during response streaming — awrite_response_to_history sets chat.message.content with a multi-block ChatMessage, triggering ValueError. Reproducible via astream_chat + get_full_response(). Affects document workflow chat_no_relevant_context path.

signals.review_reason: Batch embedding returns wrong output shape causing data corruption in RAG pipelines. SDK version upgrade introduced behavioral change that silently breaks existing code.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: GoogleGenAIEmbedding with "gemini-embedding-2" produces aggregated embeddings instead of individual ones with google-genai SDK v1.71.0+
source_issues.evidence: get_text_embedding_batch([3 strings]) returns len=1 instead of len=3 when using google-genai SDK 1.71.0+. Breaks batch embedding in RAG pipelines. Reproducible with explicit code sample.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Download of images is not possible

source_issues.title: [Bug]: google_genai produces cryptic errors for >20MB file uploads with vertexai config
source_issues.evidence: Upstream google-genai SDK returns 'This method is only supported in the Gemini Developer client' for >20MB uploads via VertexAI. LlamaIndex does not intercept and re-route to a clearer error path.

source_issues.title: [upstream] @ruvector/sona@0.1.6 is an empty publish — broke @claude-flow/neural until alpha.9 pinned around it

signals.topic: vectorBackend controller permanently disabled due to API version mismatch

signals.review_reason: Key feature (vectorBackend for semantic memory) is permanently disabled. User's explicit config_set call is silently ignored. This is not a transient failure but a permanent unavailability of a key feature.

source_issues.evidence: config_set enables vectorBackend but agentdb.getController('vectorBackend') throws 'Unknown controller: vectorBackend'. The controller is entirely unreachable. User's config change has no effect and the feature is permanently unavailable.

signals.topic: memory store/search completely broken on Windows

aliases: memory search returns nothing on Windows
signals.review_reason: Core memory functionality is completely broken on Windows — the primary OS for many users. Store appears to succeed but data is never findable. This is a significant experience degradation making the memory feature unusable on Windows.

source_issues.title: Windows: memory store succeeds but search returns no results and stats shows 0 entries (v3.7.0-alpha.27)
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 11 with v3.7.0-alpha.27: memory store prints success, but memory search returns 'No results found' and memory stats shows 'Total Entries: 0'. Reproduced with upsert/ttl/tags and after daemon restart. Also triggers libuv assertion failure.

signals.topic: pre-bash dangerous-command validation silently bypassed (security gate is no-op)

signals.review_reason: A documented security control (dangerous command validation) is a complete no-op for real Claude Code payloads. Commands that should be blocked pass through. This is a security feature failure with direct user impact for anyone relying on the hook for safety.

source_issues.title: pre-bash hook silently skips dangerous-command validation on real Claude Code payloads
source_issues.evidence: hook-handler.cjs reads the wrong field for command validation. Dangerous commands like 'rm -rf / --no-preserve-root' pass through unblocked because .toLowerCase() on an object throws, which is swallowed by the 5s safety timer. The documented security gate is completely non-functional.

signals.topic: browser_session_record fails due to missing --dimension flag, breaking entire browser tool stack
signals.summary: ruflo-browser 0.2.0's browser_session_record fails because ruvector rvf create is missing a required -d/--dimension flag. All downstream browser skills (23 tools) are inert.
signals.review_reason: A single missing CLI flag breaks the entire browser plugin ecosystem. Every browser-based skill is unreachable until this is fixed. Clear main workflow blocking for browser automation use cases.

source_issues.title: ruflo-browser 0.2.0: `browser_session_record` fails — `ruvector rvf create` missing required `-d, --dimension` flag
source_issues.evidence: Every call to browser_session_record fails with 'required option -d, --dimension not specified'.
