Entire 23-tool browser stack is inert.

signals.topic: Navigation success message lies after daemon failure — AI agents silently read wrong page content
signals.summary: After a failed `agent-browser close` that leaves the daemon in a half-dead state, subsequent `open` commands report "✓ <title>" success while actual content queries return stale page data from a previous URL. This causes silent data corruption where AI agents read content from unrelated pages, believing it to be from the intended target.
aliases: open reports success but loads stale content after daemon failure
navigation reported as success but returns wrong page content
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking + silent data corruption. The '✓ Done' success message in agent-browser is architecturally trusted by AI agent workflows. When the daemon is in a half-dead state, this message lies without error, causing the agent to read content from an entirely wrong page. This is not a cosmetic issue — it silently corrupts the agent's world model and downstream outputs.

source_issues.title: After failed close, subsequent open reports success but returns stale content from prior URL
source_issues.evidence: open reports correct target URL title but screenshot/snapshot returns content from unrelated prior pages (rustih.ru 404, Pasternak's Февраль, Blok's poetry). The success message is derived from the target URL, not the page actually loaded. Reporter states this led the agent to think the literary work being researched was Blok's love poetry instead of the Wikisource source it had explicitly opened — silent data corruption.

signals.topic: `--auto-connect` WebSocket timeout too short — blocks user/agent from approving Chrome remote debugging permission prompt
signals.summary: When using `--auto-connect`, Chrome may display a remote debugging permission prompt. The current auto-connect WebSocket verification times out after approximately 2 seconds, which is insufficient time for a human or automation agent to click 'Allow'. As a result, `--auto-connect` fails before the permission prompt can be handled, preventing the intended auto-connect workflow from completing.
aliases: auto-connect timeout too fast for permission prompt
WebSocket verification times out before Chrome permission can be approved
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for a legitimate use case (auto-connect to pre-existing Chrome for remote debugging). The 2-second timeout is too short for both human users and automated agents to interact with the permission dialog, making --auto-connect unreliable in any workflow that triggers the Chrome permission prompt.

source_issues.title: `--auto-connect` fails too quickly when Chrome asks for remote debugging permission
source_issues.evidence: Chrome remote debugging permission prompt requires user interaction within ~2 seconds or agent-browser --auto-connect fails. Reproducible: launch Chrome with remote debugging, run agent-browser --auto-connect open <URL>, Chrome shows permission prompt, if Allow is not clicked within 2s the connection fails. Screenshot evidence provided.

signals.topic: `network route --body` flag silently ignored — mock-based development workflows completely unusable
signals.summary: The `--body` flag on `network route` has no effect: intercepted requests pass through to the real backend instead of being stubbed. Root cause is a data flow disconnect between the CLI parser (stores body as a top-level field) and the daemon handler (only reads from nested 'response' object). This makes any mock-based development workflow that depends on `network route --body` completely broken by design.
aliases: network route body flag does not stub responses
route --body has no effect CLI daemon field mismatch
signals.review_reason: A core feature (`network route --body`) is completely non-functional. The flag is silently ignored with no error, causing requests to hit the real backend even when a mock body is specified. This breaks the entire mock-based development workflow that the feature is designed to support. Root cause is a clear code-level field name mismatch between parser and handler.

source_issues.title: Bug: `network route --body` has no effect — CLI parser and handler field mismatch
source_issues.evidence: Explicit reproduction steps: route '*' --body '{"mock":true}' then goto httpbin.org/get returns real response instead of mocked body. Control group: --abort flag works correctly, confirming CDP Fetch interception itself is fine. Root cause traced to cli/src/commands.rs storing body as top-level field vs cli/src/native/actions.rs reading from nested 'response' object.

signals.topic: Chrome 147 crashes with 'trap int3' in Docker environment — agent-browser unusable in containers

aliases: Chrome 147 trap int3 crash in docker
Chrome crashes in container environment SIGTRAP

The Chrome process crashes with SIGTRAP on every launch attempt. While the root cause may be a Chrome/environment interaction, agent-browser ships a specific Chrome version and is responsible for providing a working browser automation experience. This blocks an entire class of deployment scenarios.

source_issues.title: Chrome 147.0 crashes with 'trap int3' when running in docker
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash on every URL open in Docker. Coredump shows chrome process receiving SIGTRAP (trap int3). Chrome version: 147.0.7727.57. 5 comments actively discussing root cause and potential workarounds. User suspects --enable-unsafe-swiftshader flag. Docker is a critical CI/server use case.

signals.topic: AI Gateway previousResponseId fails silently for OpenAI Responses API with pooled credentials

signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking with silent state loss - any user building multi-turn conversational AI on Gateway + OpenAI Responses API will lose conversation history without warning. This is a fundamental feature of chat that fails silently.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: previousResponseId fails for OpenAI Responses API across pooled credentials
source_issues.evidence: Stateful chat using previousResponseId silently fails - the responseId round-trips successfully but persistence is non-functional because Gateway load-balances across pooled OpenAI accounts. Users lose conversation context without any error message.

signals.topic: Turbopack chunk filenames with multiple dots trigger WAF 403 responses — blocks all production deployments behind reverse proxies
signals.summary: Turbopack generates chunk filenames with 3+ dots (e.g., 0od.e4.nsryo4.js) which standard WAF rules interpret as malicious multi-extension patterns (e.g., shell.php.jpg) and return 403 Forbidden. This causes ChunkLoadError and completely breaks production deployments behind AWS WAF, Cloudflare, ModSecurity, or Azure Front Door.
aliases: turbopack chunk naming security false positive
multiple dot chunk filenames blocked by WAF
signals.review_reason: Blocks the entire production deployment workflow for any user deploying behind a standard WAF/reverse proxy (AWS WAF, Cloudflare, ModSecurity, Azure Front Door). This affects a very broad user base as WAF usage is standard enterprise/CDN practice. The app becomes completely non-functional in production with ChunkLoadError.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack generates chunk filenames like '0od.e4.nsryo4.js' (3 dots). Standard WAF rules flag these as multi-extension attack patterns and return 403. Verified: chunks with 1-2 dots return 200, chunk with 3 dots returns 403. ChunkLoadError at runtime. Affects deployments behind AWS WAF, Cloudflare, ModSecurity, Azure Front Door.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Identical root cause as #93790. Confirms 3-dot chunk filenames block deployments behind reverse proxies/WAF. Webpack generates 'chunks/framework-abc123.js' without multi-dot issue. Only Turbopack is affected.

signals.topic: ISR with turbopack silently produces incomplete RSC payload during build-time SSG prerender — pages render as hydration skeleton forever
signals.summary: Pages using generateStaticParams + revalidate with turbopack silently produce incomplete RSC payloads at build time. HTML renders (200 OK, prerender header), but page content is a hydration skeleton that never resolves. Error: 'Connection closed.' The broken payload is locked into Vercel's edge cache, persisting the failure across all requests. Caused a documented 21-hour production outage.
signals.review_reason: Caused a 21-hour production outage affecting 5 pages with zero build-time error. Users see an empty page (hydration skeleton) with no actionable error. The broken payload gets cached at Vercel's edge, locking in the failure. This is the worst possible failure mode: silent, persistent, and invisible at build time.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Next.js 16 + turbopack + ISR: silent incomplete RSC payload on SSG prerender (generateStaticParams + revalidate, production-only)
source_issues.evidence: 21-hour production outage documented on maisondetalents.com (2026-05-16). 5 pages affected: /, /brands, /brands/[slug], /guide/interview/[brand], /guide/store/[slug]. RSC payload truncated to ~184KB containing $L Suspense placeholders without resolution chunks. curl -H 'RSC: 1' confirms incomplete payload. Broken payload cached at edge (x-vercel-cache: HIT). Temporary fix: force-dynamic hotfix loses ISR benefits.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Next.js 16 + turbopack: silent incomplete RSC payload on build-time SSG prerender with generateStaticParams + revalidate (page-content dependent)
source_issues.evidence: Bisect matrix shows generateStaticParams is necessary condition; revalidate value is not the cause. Pages with GNB (next/dynamic lazy children) + JSON-LD + medium complexity are broken. Static mock of Supabase fetch still breaks — data fetch is not the cause. Local npm run build && npm start does NOT reproduce — production-only (Vercel build environment specific).

signals.topic: Next.js 16 middleware on Vercel: Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js — both middleware and page functions fail
signals.summary: On Vercel deployments with Next.js 16 and a proxy.ts middleware file, the runtime fails with 'Cannot find module /var/task/node_modules/@swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js' even though the module exists in the local install. Affects both middleware function (MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED) and page render function (FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED) execution paths.
aliases: NFT trace missing ESM module Vercel
signals.review_reason: Complete Vercel deployment failure for Next.js 16 users with middleware. Both middleware and page functions crash with 500 at runtime. Local build gives no signal of the problem. The same failure occurs in production and preview deployments, across 16.2.5 and 16.2.6.

source_issues.title: MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED on Vercel deploy: Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js — minimal repro: next@16.2.6 + proxy.ts + top-level @sentry/nextjs import
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro: create-next-app@16.2.6 + 3-line proxy.ts middleware + 'import * as Sentry from @sentry/nextjs' in instrumentation.ts. Builds locally without warnings. Deploys to Vercel → MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED and FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED. Local artifact has zero references to @swc/helpers; Vercel artifact still requests it at runtime.

source_issues.title: MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED + FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED on Vercel deploy: Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js (next 16.2.x + proxy.ts middleware)
source_issues.evidence: 5.5 hours of hypothesis falsification by reporter. Renaming proxy.ts away shifts error to FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED on / with identical stack trace, confirming the caller is framework-level, not application code. Downgrading to 16.2.5 reproduces. Local build is clean; only Vercel's deploy pipeline triggers the failure.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 SWC/Turbopack build hangs indefinitely — deterministic deadlock in compile orchestrator
signals.summary: Production builds hang at 100% CPU in the SWC compile phase with no timeout signal, reproducible on macOS arm64 AND Linux x86_64 (Vercel cloud) with both Turbopack and webpack, across Next.js 16.0.0 to 16.3.0-canary.19. Builds cannot complete; process must be manually killed.
signals.review_reason: Main production workflow (next build) is completely blocked for all Next.js 16 users across platforms. The deadlock is deterministic (byte-exact trace size across runs), affects both bundlers, and has no in-band error signal — only manual process kill resolves it. Bisect confirms it is a regression from Next.js 15 to 16.

source_issues.title: next build hangs indefinitely in SWC compile phase on Next 16 (next dev works) — reproduces on macOS arm64 AND Linux x86_64 (Vercel cloud)
source_issues.evidence: Build hangs at 'Creating an optimized production build...' with zero further output. CPU pinned at 100% on 2 worker processes. .next/trace freezes at exactly 107,831,441 bytes (deterministic across runs). Stack trace shows Tokio runtime threads 1900+ frames deep inside next-swc binary. Bisect confirmed: next@15.5.18 works, next@16.0.0 hangs. Both Turbopack and webpack affected. Both macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 (Vercel cloud) affected.

signals.topic: Turbopack production build emits chunks referenced by page.js but missing from disk — non-deterministic 500 errors in production
signals.summary: Turbopack build reports success but omits chunks that are referenced by emitted page.js files. This causes intermittent 500 errors (ChunkLoadError, client reference manifest missing) at runtime in a non-deterministic manner that changes across rebuilds, making it extremely dangerous for CI/CD pipelines.
signals.review_reason: Build claims success but produces invalid artifacts that cause 500 errors at runtime. The non-deterministic nature (which routes fail changes per rebuild) makes this extremely dangerous for CI/CD — a build can pass all checks and then 500 in production. This blocks the core production deployment workflow.

source_issues.title: next build (Turbopack) emits page.js with references to chunks that are missing on disk — non-deterministic across rebuilds
source_issues.evidence: Build succeeds and prints clean route summary, but .next/server/chunks/ssr/ is missing chunks referenced by app/page.js files. Symptom manifests as ChunkLoadError (Cannot find module) and InvariantError (client reference manifest missing). Failures shift across FR/EN routes on each fresh build. Request-order dependent, making CI detection difficult. App Router + Turbopack + next-intl locale segments.

signals.topic: JSON schema URL returns 404 in IDE after turbo version upgrade, blocking schema validation in VSCode
signals.summary: When turbo.json references a pinned schema URL like https://v2-9-14.turborepo.dev/schema.json, the URL returns 404 after version upgrade, causing VSCode JSON validation to fail with 'DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND' errors. Users must manually update schema URLs to restore validation.
aliases: schema validation broken after version upgrade
signals.review_reason: This is a DX-blocking issue: schema validation in the IDE breaks after any turbo version upgrade when users have pinned schema URLs, causing persistent JSON squiggle errors and lost autocompletion. Multiple users affected as confirmed by the error path containing the versioned schema URL.

source_issues.title: Unable to load schema from "https://v2-9-14.turborepo.dev/schema.json"
source_issues.evidence: Users encounter 'Unable to load schema' error in VSCode JSON validation after turbo version upgrade; the schema URL returns DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND from Vercel deployment, breaking IDE schema validation and autocompletion for turbo.json.

signals.topic: Turbo fails to resolve workspaces with pnpm v11 devEngines.packageManager field
signals.summary: pnpm v11 introduced devEngines.packageManager as the preferred field over packageManager. Turbo does not recognize devEngines.packageManager, causing 'Missing packageManager field in package.json' errors and workspace resolution failure when running turbo tasks with pnpm v11.
signals.review_reason: This is a monorepo workflow blocker: users upgrading to pnpm v11 cannot run any turbo tasks due to workspace resolution failure, completely breaking the primary use case. Clear user impact with exact error messages and reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: support `devEngines` with pnpm v11
source_issues.evidence: Running 'turbo run check-types' with pnpm v11 fails with 'Could not resolve workspaces: Missing packageManager field in package.json' because pnpm v11 uses devEngines.packageManager, which Turbo does not recognize.

signals.topic: TUI pipe border character gets captured in VSCode terminal links, making file paths unclickable
signals.summary: The turbo TUI left border pipe character (│) is adjacent to task output without whitespace separation. VSCode terminal treats the pipe as part of file paths and URLs, causing turbo's own output links (e.g., 'apps/app-a/repro.js:2') to be unclickable in the VSCode integrated terminal. Workaround requires pressing 'h' to hide the task list panel.
aliases: TUI links unclickable in VSCode terminal
pipe character breaks clickable links in TUI
signals.review_reason: Significant DX regression that breaks a core turbo TUI interaction: file path links in turbo's own output become unclickable in VSCode (one of the most popular IDEs). The workaround of pressing 'h' is disruptive for teams that rely on TUI + VSCode terminal daily. Clear reproduction with screenshots.

source_issues.title: Lack of whitespace after the TUI task output left border causes "stuck pipe character" in links opened from VSCode Terminal
source_issues.evidence: VSCode terminal parses '│path/to/file.ext' as a single link including the pipe character, making turbo's own output file references unclickable. User states this is a 'huge pain point' at their company where TUI is used extensively. Screenshots confirm broken link parsing.

signals.topic: Race condition: turbo signals task complete before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendants leave the tracked process group
signals.summary: When a task spawns a subprocess that exits the task's tracked process group (via detached:true, setsid, or double-fork), turbo prematurely signals task completion. Dependent tasks are immediately scheduled and fail with 'Could not resolve' because output files are not yet written. Affects real-world build chains using bunx --bun with Node CLIs that spawn detached workers.
aliases: WARNING no output files found race condition
signals.review_reason: This is a critical main-flow blocker: turbo incorrectly signals task completion before output files are written, causing dependent tasks to fail with module resolution errors. The race is deterministic in synthetic tests and affects real-world build chains (Prisma/generator CLIs with bunx). Confirmed by Turbo maintainer with a fix PR already merged. P0 due to main-flow impact and 99.5-100% reproduction rate in specific subprocess patterns.

source_issues.title: Task signaled complete before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendants leave the tracked process group
source_issues.evidence: Synthetic test shows 99.5-100% failure rate for detached/double-fork subprocess patterns. Real-world bunx --bun CLIs fail at ~1.2% on Linux CI. Turbo prints 'WARNING no output files found for task' and dependent tasks fail with module resolution errors.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker produces invalid output with literal workspace definitions, causing bun install to fail in Docker builds
signals.summary: When package.json contains literal workspace definitions (array of package paths) alongside glob patterns, turbo prune generates an incorrect pruned package.json that references non-existent packages. Subsequent 'bun install' in the Docker image fails with 'Workspace not found' errors, breaking Docker build pipelines.
aliases: turbo prune bun install workspace not found
turbo prune broken with literal workspace arrays
signals.review_reason: This blocks a critical production workflow: Docker container builds using 'turbo prune --docker' fail entirely when package.json uses literal workspace definitions. Build pipelines are completely broken with clear error messages from bun install. Also impacts catalog support for pnpm.

source_issues.title: literal workspaces + `turbo prune --docker` + `bun install` fails
source_issues.evidence: Docker build pipeline fails with 'Workspace not found' errors when using turbo prune output with bun install. The issue is reproducible: globs-only workspaces work correctly, but mixing literal and glob workspace definitions causes turbo prune to generate invalid pruned package.json.

signals.topic: Services-mode (experimentalServices) with middleware.ts causes deterministic deploy failure at 'Deploying outputs' stage
signals.summary: When a project uses `experimentalServices` with a non-root service and has a `middleware.ts`, every deployment fails deterministically at the 'Deploying outputs' stage with a generic 'unexpected error' message. The root cause is that middleware routes are not exempted from `scopeRoutesToServiceOwnership` — the ownership guard rewrites the middleware route's `src` regex, corrupting it. The workaround is to drop middleware.ts or stay on `framework: nextjs`, but the combination is completely broken.
aliases: middleware routes scoped incorrectly in services-mode
signals.review_reason: This is a high-impact deploy-blocking bug. The services-mode + middleware combination causes deterministic, reproducible deployment failures with a generic opaque error message. Production workflows are blocked with no permanent fix available — users must either remove middleware.ts (breaking their app's auth/routing logic) or abandon services-mode entirely. Vercel internal support cases confirm real customer impact. This meets the P0 bar: main flow is blocked, count=1 is acceptable because the root cause is structurally deterministic (every such project would fail) and the underlying bug is confirmed.

source_issues.title: Services-Mode: Middleware routes are not exempted from scopeRoutesToServiceOwnership, breaking deploy outputs
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic failure in minimal 5-file sandbox combining experimentalServices + middleware.ts. Generic error 'An unexpected error occurred when running this build' at 'Deploying outputs' stage. Isolated root cause: `scopeRoutesToServiceOwnership` rewrites middleware route `src` with ownership guard but middleware routes carry `middlewarePath` (not `handle`), so the exemption is missed. Confirmed by Vercel internal support cases (01kpgVUAoxBA9kuW, 01161162) and community threads. Workaround available but not a fix.

signals.topic: vercel env add with --sensitive --value --yes silently saves empty string, causing production 500 errors
signals.summary: The CLI command `vercel env add NAME --sensitive --yes --value <V>` returns a success message with exit code 0 but stores the variable with an empty value. The `vercel env ls` UI shows it as 'Encrypted' (appearing healthy), but `vercel env pull` reveals length 0. This silently breaks production deployments — functions receiving the var get empty strings and 500, often after hours of confusion.
aliases: sensitive env var save silently empty
vercel env add sensitive flag data corruption
signals.review_reason: This is silent data corruption with confirmed production impact. The CLI reports success while corrupting the stored value, making diagnosis extremely difficult. The UI masks the problem by showing the var as 'Encrypted' (appears healthy). Production functions receive empty strings and return 500 errors. The author explicitly describes spending hours confused before discovering the root cause. This meets the P0 bar: key functionality is silently broken, causing production failures with no error signal.

source_issues.title: vercel env add --value V --sensitive --yes silently saves empty string
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed across CLI versions 50.42.0 and 51.6.1. Reproduces with shell-quoted and Python-subprocess-argv invocations (not bash mangling). Silent data corruption: command reports success (exit 0), UI shows 'Encrypted' (looks healthy), but actual stored value is empty string. Production functions receiving the var 500 with no indication the var is empty. Hours of debugging before root cause found. Workaround: drop --sensitive flag.

signals.topic: vercel logs pagination returns duplicate entries when crossing page boundary (>50 results)
signals.summary: The CLI command `vercel logs --since <window> --json --limit N` returns duplicate entries when the time window contains more than 50 log entries. The first page of 50 results is fetched correctly; every subsequent page returns the same first page again. The CLI accumulates duplicates until --limit is reached. The server-side `/api/logs/?page=N` endpoint appears to ignore the page parameter.
aliases: vercel logs CLI returns same page repeatedly
signals.review_reason: A CLI command produces incorrect results deterministically when the result set exceeds one page. Log analysis is a core observability workflow; duplicates make the output unreliable and can mislead developers debugging production issues. The bug is confirmed reproducible and the root cause (server-side pagination ignoring page parameter) is well-reasoned. Impact is real but not blocking the main deploy flow — P1 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: vercel logs returns duplicate entries when there are more than 50 results and --limit > 50
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction verified with shell commands: `--since 7min` (fits in one page) → 28/28 unique; `--since 10min` (crosses page boundary) → 100/50 unique (first page duplicated); `--since 12h` → 100/50 unique. Duplicates are byte-identical with same id and timestamp. Root cause suspected server-side: pagination endpoint ignores `?page=N` while still reporting `pagination.hasMore: true`. CLI pagination loop is structurally correct.

signals.topic: DEP0040 punycode deprecation warning fires on every Vercel hosted build and cannot be silenced from user side
signals.summary: The Node 22 DEP0040 punycode deprecation warning fires on every `vercel build` in Vercel's hosted build environment. The suggested user-side workarounds (NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1, vercel.json build.env, dashboard env vars) do not reach the launcher Node process itself, only the user build subprocesses. Users have no mechanism to suppress launcher-level warnings in hosted builds.
aliases: punycode deprecation warning in vercel build
DEP0040 warning cannot be silenced hosted builds
signals.review_reason: The deprecation warning fires on every single hosted build with no user-side workaround, making it a persistent UX nuisance across all Vercel users. While it doesn't block deploys, it pollutes build logs, may mask real warnings, and signals that the Vercel CLI's bundled dependencies have not been updated to remove deprecated Node builtins — a maintenance debt with potential future breakage risk. The follow-up nature (#11905 was closed with a promise unfulfilled) adds urgency. P1 appropriate (not blocking main flow, but significant and universal).

source_issues.title: [CLI] DEP0040 punycode warning persists in hosted builds — user env vars don't reach launcher (follow-up to #11905)
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic on every `vercel build` in Vercel hosted environment (CLI 53.3.2, Node 22). Warning fires ~7ms before CLI banner during launcher bootstrap. `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1` and dashboard `NODE_OPTIONS` both confirmed empirically not to reach launcher process. Tracked as a follow-up to #11905 (closed Aug 2024 with promise to remove punycode dependency during Node 22 upgrade — promise not yet fulfilled). Root cause: bare `require('punycode')` in multiple bundled packages resolves to deprecated Node builtin.

signals.topic: Vercel Security Checkpoint false positives block legitimate visitors without a public reporting channel
signals.summary: Legitimate visitors are blocked by 'Failed to verify your browser Code 11 Vercel Security Checkpoint' when visiting Vercel-protected sites. There is no public mechanism to report false positives — visitors are directed to the sales contact form, which is inappropriate for security false-positive reporting. Legitimate users are locked out of sites with no recourse.
aliases: Vercel security checkpoint false positive no reporting
signals.review_reason: Security checkpoint false positives blocking legitimate visitors is a real user-facing service access issue. Without a reporting channel, affected site owners cannot learn about or fix false positives affecting their users. This is distinct from a security vulnerability — it is a service usability failure where the anti-bot mechanism incorrectly blocks real users and provides no remediation path. The impact on both end visitors and site owners is clear. P1 appropriate.

source_issues.title: False positive "Failed to verify your browser Code 11 Vercel Security Checkpoint"
source_issues.evidence: Reporter was legitimately blocked from accessing https://docs.arbitrum.io/run-arbitrum-node/overview. Attempted to search Vercel contact options and found only the sales contact form, which is not appropriate for false-positive security reports. No public bug bounty program or security false-positive reporting channel exists. The visitor has no path to regain access to the legitimate content.

signals.topic: Suggestion/completion system returns incorrect ranked results, leading to destructive actions and lost user work
signals.summary: The fuzzy-search suggestion ranking algorithm consistently misranks results. The most relevant match (exact prefix match) is ranked lower than a far less relevant fuzzy match, causing the wrong item to be auto-selected and resulting in destructive actions (e.g. opening wrong file, executing wrong command) that have already caused data loss.
signals.review_reason: User impact is explicit and severe: suggestions consistently misrank and have caused lost work. The destructive nature of the top-ranked wrong suggestion meets the 'user pain point' bar despite count=1, as the evidence of repeated occurrence ('consistently off', 'a few times') and clear data-loss impact make this a confirmed UX bug.

source_issues.title: Suggestions weight is consistently off
source_issues.evidence: User reports suggestions consistently rank worse matches above exact prefix matches; the wrong suggestion is also destructive and has already caused data loss ('has already cost me my work a few times'). Affects all suggestion types including file suggestions and inline suggestions.

signals.topic: Cloudflare WAF blocks VPN users from signing in to Zed, making the app unusable for a significant user segment
signals.summary: Cloudflare's bot protection on zed.dev returns HTTP 403 for users connecting via VPN in certain regions (e.g. Mexico), blocking both web access and desktop app sign-in. This is a hard authentication failure that completely prevents use of the product for affected users.
signals.review_reason: User impact is complete authentication failure: users cannot sign in to Zed at all when using a VPN in certain regions, making the entire application unusable. The evidence includes full HTTP 403 response body and error log showing 'failed to validate credentials: Failed to get authenticated user. Status: 403'. This is a hard block on the primary user onboarding/auth flow.

source_issues.title: Cloudflare blocks zed.dev when connected to a VPN service in Mexico
source_issues.evidence: Cloudflare returns HTTP 403 on auth endpoint for VPN users in Mexico. Both Zed website and desktop app sign-in are blocked. Error log confirms: 'Status: 403, Body: Attention Required! Cloudflare'. Affects users in corporate VPN environments.

signals.topic: REPL hangs indefinitely when connecting to Jupyter kernels that defer stdin socket binding (e.g. IHaskell)
signals.summary: Zed's REPL attempts to connect to the Jupyter kernel's stdin socket immediately on startup, but kernels like IHaskell bind the stdin socket late (after other sockets), causing Zed to hang indefinitely on 'Connecting to kernel'. This blocks the entire REPL feature for affected kernel types.
signals.review_reason: User impact is indefinite hang of a core feature (REPL) with no recovery. The issue is confirmed reproducible (state:reproducible), has a root cause analysis showing Zed's kernel connection logic races against late-binding stdin sockets, and blocks the entire REPL use case for a class of Jupyter kernels.

source_issues.title: REPL hangs on Jupyter kernels that don't bind a stdin socket at start up (e.g. IHaskell)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: install IHaskell kernel, open .hs file in Zed, start REPL, run cell -> hangs indefinitely on 'Connecting to kernel'. Same kernel works in jupyter console. Root cause: IHaskell binds stdin port last; Zed connects immediately and sees ECONNREFUSED then hangs. State is reproducible and documented.
